semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {فِي بُيُوتٍ}: there are six views on it. First: that it is a ṣifa (adjective) of «مِشْكاةٍ», meaning: like a niche in houses, that is, in a house among the houses of Allah. Second: that it is a ṣifa of «مصباح». Third: that it is a ṣifa of «زجاجة». Fourth: that it is attached to «تُوْقَدُ». On these views one does not pause at «عليم». Fifth: that it is attached to an omitted element, like His saying {فِي تِسْعِ آيَاتٍ} [النمل: 12], meaning: they glorify Him in houses. Sixth: that it is attached to «يُسَبِّحُ», meaning: men glorify Him in houses. It contains a repetition for emphasis, like His saying: {فَفِي الجنة خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا} [هود: 108]. On these two views one pauses at «عليم». The Shaykh said: "On these three views", though only two views were mentioned.
His saying: {أَذِنَ الله} is in the position of genitive as a ṣifa of «بيوتٍ», and «أن تُرفع» is on the omission of the preposition, that is: «في أَنْ تُرْفَعَ». It is not permissible for «في بيوت» to be attached to His saying «ويُذْكَرُ», because that is conjoined to what falls within the scope of «أَنْ», and what follows «أَنْ» cannot precede it.
His saying: {يُسَبِّحُ}: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read it with fatḥa on the bāʾ, as a passive.
The deputy agent is one of the three genitive phrases. The first of them is the most suitable for this, because the verb needs its nominative, and the one that comes next to it has priority. On this reading «رجالٌ» is nominative in one of two ways: either by an implied verb, since it is impossible to attribute the verb to it [as agent], and it is as if it were the answer to an implied question, as though it had been said: "Who glorifies Him?" and it was said: "Men glorify Him." On this, in one of the two analyses, is the poet's verse:
3448 - لِيُبْكَ يََزِيْدُ ضارعٌ لخُصُومَةٍ ... ومُخْتَبِطٌ مِمَّا تُطيحُ الطَّوائحُ
(Let Yazīd be wept for by one humbled before a dispute, and by a beggar ruined by what calamities destroy.)
as if it had been said: "Who weeps for him?" and it was said: "One humbled weeps for him." However, there is disagreement over whether this may be taken as a general rule: some allowed it and some forbade it. The second analysis of the verse: that «يَزيدُ» is a vocative whose vocative particle has been omitted, that is: "O Yazīd", and this is very weak.
The second: that «رجالاً» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is: "the one who glorifies Him is men". On this reading one pauses at «الآصال».
The rest of the Seven read it with kasra on the bāʾ, as an active verb. The agent is «رجال», so one does not pause at «الآصال».
Ibn Wathāb and Abū Ḥaywa read «تُسَبِّح» with tāʾ (two dots above) and kasra on the bāʾ, because a broken plural is treated like the feminine in some rulings, and this is one of them. Abū Jaʿfar read it likewise except that he put fatḥa on the bāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī analysed it as the verb being attributed to «الغُدُوّ والآصال» with the bāʾ being redundant, as in their saying: «صِيْد عليه يومان» ("two days of hunting were spent upon him"), that is, its wild game.
Others analysed it as the deputy agent being the pronoun of the tasbīḥa (act of glorification), that is: "the glorification is glorified", by the figurative usage that permits attributing it to the two times, just as they analysed Abū Jaʿfar's reading too of {ليجزى قَوْماً بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكْسِبُونَ} [الجاثية: 14], that is: "that recompense be recompensed to a people". Indeed this one is better than the verse in al-Jāthiya, since here there is no explicit direct object.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {لاَّ تُلْهِيهِمْ}: in the position of nominative, as a ṣifa (adjective) of «رجالٌ».
His saying: {يَخَافُونَ}: it may be a second naʿt (adjective) of «رجال», and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «تُلْهِيْهم». «يوماً» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and not a circumstantial adverb, according to the more apparent view. «يتقلَّبُ» is a ṣifa of «يوماً».

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {لِيَجْزِيَهُمُ}: it may be attached to «يُسَبِّح», meaning: they glorify for the sake of the recompense. It may also be attached to an omitted element, meaning: they did that so that He might recompense them. The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words is that this belongs to the chapter of iʿmāl (the competing of two operators for one object), for he said: "The meaning is: they glorify and fear, so that He may recompense them", and it is based on giving effect to the second operator, with omission from the first.
His saying: {أَحْسَنَ مَا عَمِلُواْ}, meaning: the reward of the best of, or the best recompense of, what they did. «ما» is either maṣdarī (forming a verbal noun) or has the meaning of «الذي» (the one who/that which), an indefinite one. [Translator's note: the source text says «أنكرة»; this is probably a misprint for «نكرة» ("indefinite"), but it is translated as written.]

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {بِقِيعَةٍ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is attached to an omitted element, being a ṣifa (adjective) of «سراب». The second: that it is a ẓarf (adverbial), and the operator in it is the "being" (istiqrār) that operates in the kāf of comparison. As-sarāb (mirage) is what appears to a person in the wilderness in intense heat, resembling water. It is also said: it is what condenses in the depths of the low-lying plains. The poet said: 3449 - فلَّما كَفَفَتُ الحربَ كانَتْ عهودُكُمْ ... كَلَمْعِ سَرابٍ في الفَلا مُتَأَلِّقِ
(When I held back the war, your covenants were like the glitter of a mirage shimmering in the desert.)
It is used as a proverb for one who expects good of something and is then disappointed. / It is also said: it is the radiance that the midday sun casts in intense heat, which appears to the observer to be flowing (sārib) water, that is, running water. Al-qīʿa has the meaning of al-qāʿ, which is the flat expanse of the earth. This was already discussed in Ṭā Hā. It is also said: rather, it is its plural, like jār and jīza. [Translator's note: the source text reads «جارٍ وجِيْزَة»; it is translated as written.]
Maslama ibn Muḥārib read it with an elongated tāʾ (tāʾ mamṭūṭa). It is also reported from him with a tāʾ in the shape of a hāʾ, and he pauses on it with a hāʾ. There are several analyses of it. The first: that it has the meaning of «قِيْعَة» like the majority reading, and the fatḥa was merely lengthened so that an alif was generated from it, as in «مُخْرَنْبِقٌ ليَنْباعَ»; this is what the author of al-Lawāmiḥ said. The second: that it is a plural of «قِيْعَة», and he paused on it with hāʾ following the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ in their saying: «الإِخْوةُ والأخواهْ، ودَفْنُ البناهُ مِنْ المَكْرُماهُ», meaning: "and the sisters, and the burying of daughters is among the noble deeds" (al-akhawāt, al-banāt, al-makrumāt). This reading supports the view that «قِيْعَة» is a plural of «قاع». The third: al-Zamakhsharī said: "and the saying of some of them: «بقيعاة» with a round tāʾ, like «رجلٍ عِزْهاة»" (a man averse to women). The apparent sense of this is that he made this an independent form, neither a plural nor an extension of usage.
His saying: {يَحْسَبُهُ الظمآن} is a clause in the position of genitive, also as a ṣifa of «سَراب». That is made good by the preposition-phrase preceding the clause; this holds if we make the preposition-phrase a ṣifa. The nominative pronouns in «جاءَه», in «لم يَجِدْه» and in «وَجَد», and the pronouns in «عنده», in «وَفَّاه» and in «حسابه» all refer to «الظمآن», because what is meant by him is the disbeliever mentioned first. This is the view of al-Zamakhsharī and it is good. It is also said: rather, the two pronouns in «جاءه» and «وجد» refer to «الظمآن», while the others refer to the disbeliever. The pronoun is singular on this view even though a plural precedes it, namely His saying {والذين كفروا}, by construing it according to the sense, since the meaning is: each one of the disbelievers. The first is preferable because of the consistency of the pronouns.
Abū Jaʿfar read, and it is reported from Nāfiʿ also, «الظَّمان» by transferring the vowel of the hamza onto the mīm.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {والطير}: the majority read «والطيرُ» in the nominative and «صافاتٍ» in the accusative: the nominative is conjoined to «مَنْ» and the accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Aʿraj read «والطيرَ» in the accusative as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), and «صافَّاتٍ» is also a ḥāl. Al-Ḥasan and Khārija, from Nāfiʿ, read «والطيرُ صافَّاتٌ» with both in the nominative, as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The object of «صافَّاتٌ» is omitted, that is: its wings.
His saying: {كُلٌّ قَدْ عَلِمَ صَلاَتَهُ}: there are several views about these pronouns. One: that all of them refer to «كل», that is: each has known its own prayer and its own glorification. This is preferable because of the agreement of the pronouns. The second: that the pronoun in «عَلِمَ» refers to Allah the Exalted, and that in «صلاتَه وتسبيحَه» refers to «كل». The third: the reverse, that is: each has known Allah's prayer and glorification, meaning: He commanded both and commanded that they be performed, as creation is ascribed to the Creator.
Abū al-Baqāʾ preferred that the agent be the pronoun of «كل». He said: "Because the reading has «كلٌّ» in the nominative as mubtadaʾ, so the pronoun of the agent returns to it; and if it contained the pronoun of the name of Allah, it would have been preferable to put «كل» in the accusative, because the verb after it has already governed what is connected with it, so it becomes like your saying: «زيداً ضربَ عمروٌ غلامَه», where you put «زيداً» in the accusative by a verb indicated by what comes after it, and that is stronger than the nominative, though the other is permissible." I say: it is not as he mentioned, in preferring the accusative over the nominative in this case, nor in this sūra. Rather the grammarians stated explicitly that in a case like this the nominative by ibtidāʾ (inchoative) is preferred over the accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation), because there is no indicator among the indicators that they made grounds for preferring the accusative, and the accusative requires an implied verb whereas the nominative does not require it, so it is the preferred one.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ}: there are several views on it. First: that it is a conjunction (nasaq) on «كسَراب», with the omission of a single muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct), whose implied form is: "or like the possessor of darknesses". What indicates this muḍāf is His saying: {إِذَآ أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا}, for the pronoun refers to the omitted muḍāf. This is the view of Abū ʿAlī. Second: that it involves the omission of two muḍāfs, whose implied form is: "or like the deeds of the possessor of darknesses"; you imply «ذي» so that the pronoun may validly refer to it in His saying {إِذَآ أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ}, and you imply «أعمال» so that the comparison of the disbelievers' deeds with the deeds of the one in darkness is valid, since there is no sense in comparing a deed to the one in darkness. Third: that there is no need for any omission at all. The meaning is that He compared the deeds of the disbelievers, in their coming between the heart and what guides it, to darkness. As for the two pronouns in «أَخْرج يَده», they refer to an omitted element indicated by the meaning, that is: when the one who is in them brings out his hand.
«أو» here is for classification, not for doubt. It is also said: rather, it is for option, that is: they compared their deeds to this or to this.
Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn read «أوَ كظٌلُمات» with fatḥa on the wāw, making it a conjunction onto which the interrogative hamza has entered, whose meaning is affirmation (taqrīr). This was discussed earlier in His saying: {أَوَ أَمِنَ أَهْلُ القرى} [الأعراف: 98].
His saying: {فِي بَحْرٍ لُّجِّيٍّ}: «في بحرٍ» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «ظلمات», so it is attached to an omitted element. «اللُّجِّيُّ» is a nisba (relative adjective) from «اللُّجّ», which is the main body of the sea. Thus al-Zamakhsharī said. Others said: it is related to «اللُجَّة» with tāʾ, which also means its main body, so «اللجِّيُّ» is the deep one with abundant water.
His saying: {يَغْشَاهُ مَوْجٌ} is another ṣifa of «بَحْرٍ», if we return the pronoun in «يَغْشاه» to «بحرٍ», and that is the apparent view. If we imply an omitted muḍāf, that is, "or like the possessor of darknesses", as some have done, then the pronoun in «يَغْشاه» would refer to it, and the clause would be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, because it is specified by the genitive construct, or a ṣifa of it.
His saying: {مِّن فَوْقِهِ مَوْجٌ}: it may be a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar, a ṣifa of the first «موجٌ». It may also be that only the preposition and its genitive noun are made the description, with «مَوْجٌ» an agent of it, because of its reliance on the described noun.
His saying: {مِّن فَوْقِهِ سَحَابٌ}: it has the two views mentioned before it: that the clause is a ṣifa of the second «موج», or only the preposition-phrase.
His saying: {ظُلُمَاتٌ}: the majority read it in the nominative, and there are two views on it. The better: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, whose implied form is: "these", or "those are darknesses". The second: that «ظُلُمات» is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause of His saying «بعضُها فوقَ بعض» is its khabar. Al-Ḥawfī mentioned it. It is open to question, because there is no justification for beginning with this indefinite noun, unless it is said that it is described by implication, that is: "many dense darknesses", like their saying: «السَّمْنُ مَنَوَانِ بدرهم» ("ghee, two manns for a dirham").
Ibn Kathīr read «ظلماتٍ» in the genitive, except that al-Bazzī reported from him in that case the omission of the tanwīn from «سَحاب», so al-Bazzī read from him «سحابُ ظلماتٍ», making «سَحابُ» muḍāf to «ظلمات».
Qunbul reported from him the tanwīn on «سَحابٌ» like the group, together with the genitive on «ظُلُماتٍ». As for al-Bazzī's transmission, Abū al-Baqāʾ said: / "He made the piled-up wave equivalent to the cloud." As for Qunbul's transmission, he made «ظلماتٍ» a badal (substitute) for the first «ظلماتٍ».
His saying: {بَعْضُهَا فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ} is a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar, in the position of nominative or [genitive], as a khabar, according to the two readings of «ظلمات» before it, because it is a ṣifa of it. [Translator's note: the source says «في موضع رفع أو خبر»; translated as written, the sense being that it is either a khabar or a ṣifa depending on the reading.] Al-Ḥawfī allowed, on the reading with «ظلماتٌ» in the nominative, that «بعضُها» be a badal of «ظلمات». It was rejected in respect of meaning, since the meaning is to inform that they are darknesses, and that some of those darknesses are above others, describing them as piled up; not that the meaning is merely that some of those darknesses are above others, without informing that those preceding darknesses are piled-up darknesses. This too is open to question, since there is no difference between your saying «بعضُ الظلماتِ فوقَ بعض» and your saying «الظلماتُ بعضُها فوقَ بعضٍ», even if such a difference appears at first sight.
The discussion of «كاد» has already preceded, including that some claimed that its negation is affirmation and its affirmation is negation. The proofs for that were given in al-Baqara, which spares repeating it. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "«لم يَكَدْ يَراها» is an emphasis on «لم يرها», that is: he did not come near to seeing it, let alone see it. From it is the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
3450 - إذا غَيَّر النَّأْيُ المُحِبِّيْنَ لم يَكَدْ ... رَسِيْسُ الهوى مِنْ حُبِّ مَيَّةَ يَبْرَحُ
(When distance changes lovers, the lingering trace of passion for Mayya's love scarcely departs.)
that is: it did not come near to departing, so how could it depart?" Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "People differed over the interpretation of this speech. The source of the disagreement is that the basic sense of «كاد», when negated, is the occurrence of the action. Most exegetes hold that the meaning is that he does not see his hand. On this there are three analyses in the implied form. The first: that the implied form is: 'he did not see it, and he did not nearly', as a group of grammarians mentioned. This is an error, because His saying «لم يَرَها» is a categorical negation of seeing, and His saying «لم يَكَدْ», if taken according to the requirement of the chapter, would have the implied form: 'and he did not nearly see it', as is stated explicitly in the verse. If this speaker means that he did not nearly see it, and that he saw it after effort, he contradicts himself, because he negated the seeing and then affirmed it. And if the meaning of «لم يكَدْ يَراها» is: 'he did not see it at all', against the majority view in this chapter, then it should be taken that way without implying «لم يَرَها». The second analysis: that «كاد» is redundant, which is far-fetched. The third: that «كاد» is used here in the sense of «قارب» (to come near), and the meaning is: he did not come near seeing it, and if he did not come near it he kept far from it.
On this came the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
إذا غَيَّر النَّأْيُ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
the verse; that is: it did not come near to departing. From here it is related of Dhū al-Rumma that when he was questioned about this verse, he said: I did not find [a substitute] in place of «لم يَكَدْ». The second meaning: that he saw it after effort. The comparison on this is sound, because with the intensity of the darkness, when he sharpens his gaze at his hand and brings it close to his eye, he sees it." End of quotation.
As for the first analysis, which he mentioned as the view of most, namely that it is an affirmation: it has already been stated that it is not correct and is not the view of most; what misled them in that was the verse of al-Baqara. And what we recited from some of them as a riddle is:
3451 - أَنْحْوِيَّ هذا العصرِ ماهي لفظَةٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
the two verses. As for what he mentioned about the redundancy of «كاد», that is the view of Abū Bakr and others, but it is rejected by them. As for what he mentioned as the second meaning, that he saw it after effort, that is the school of al-Farrāʾ and al-Mubarrad. And it is astonishing how he turns away from the meaning al-Zamakhsharī pointed to, namely the emphasis in negating the seeing.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said something to this effect: "When the verb after «كاد» is negated, it indicates its occurrence, as in «كاد زيدٌ لا يقوم» ('Zayd nearly did not stand'); or when affirmed it indicates its non-occurrence, as in «كاد زيد يقوم» ('Zayd nearly stood'). When the negation precedes «كاد», it may be affirmative or negative. You say: «المفلوج لا يَكاد يَسْكُن» ('the paralysed man scarcely keeps still'), which includes the negation of stillness. And you say: a man who has turned away «لا يكاد يَسْكُن», which includes the affirmation of stillness after effort."

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His saying: {بَيْنَهُ}: «بينَ» has entered a singular, although it enters only a dual or more, because either the genus is meant by «السحاب» (cloud), so the pronoun returns to it according to its ruling, or an omitted muḍāf is intended, that is: between its pieces, since every piece is a cloud.
His saying: {يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلاَلِهِ}: the disagreement over «خِلال» has already been given, whether it is a singular like «حِجاب» or a plural like «جِبال», plural of «جَبَل». The first is supported by the reading of Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and it is also reported from Abū ʿAmr: «مِنْ خَلَلِه» in the singular.
Al-wadq, it is said, is rain, whether light or heavy. He said:
3452 - فلا مُزْنَةٌ وَدَقَتْ وَدْقَها ... ولا أرضَ أَبْقَلَ إبْقالَها
(No rain-cloud poured its rain, and no land put forth vegetation as hers did.)
It is also said: it is lightning. And he recited:
3453 - أَثَرْنَ عَجاجةً وخَرَجْنَ منها ... خُروج الوَدْقِ مِنْ خَلَلِ السَّحابِ
(They stirred up dust and came out of it, as the wadq comes out from the gaps of the cloud.)
Al-wadq is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); one says: «وَدَقَ السحابُ يَدِقُ وَدْقاً». «يَخْرجُ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the seeing is visual (baṣariyya).
His saying: {مِنَ السمآء مِن جِبَالٍ فِيهَا مِن بَرَدٍ}: the first «مِن» is for the beginning of the range, by agreement. As for the second, there are three views on it. First: that it too is for the beginning of the range, so it and its genitive noun are a badal (substitute) for the first, with repetition of the operator. The implied form is: "and He sends down from the mountains of the sky", that is, from mountains in it; so it is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion). Second: that it is partitive (tabʿīḍ), as said by al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya. On this it and its genitive noun are in the position of the object of the sending down, as if he had said: "and He sends down some mountains". Third: that it is redundant, that is: "He sends down mountains from the sky". Al-Ḥawfī said: "«مِنْ جبال» is a badal of the first." Then he said: "and it is partitive."
The Shaykh rejected it, saying: substitution is only correct if the two are alike in meaning. If you said «خَرَجْتُ من بغدادَ من الكَرْخِ» ("I left Baghdad, from al-Karkh"), the first and the second could only be for the beginning of the range.
As for the third, there are four views on it: the three preceding, and a fourth: that it is for clarifying the genus (bayān al-jins). Al-Ḥawfī and al-Zamakhsharī said this, so the implied form according to them is: "and He sends down from the sky some of the mountains, which are hail", so what is sent down is hail, because some hail is hail. The object of «يُنَزِّلُ» is «مِنْ جبال», as its exposition has preceded. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or the first two are for the beginning, and the third is partitive." I say: he means that the second is a badal of the first as already explained; then the object of «يُنَزِّل» is the third with its genitive noun, its implied form being: "and He sends down some hail from the sky, from its mountains". If it is said that the second and the third are redundant, are their genitive nouns in the position of accusative, with the second a badal of the first, the implied form being "and He sends down from the sky mountains of hail", which is a badal of the whole for the whole, or of a part for the whole; or is the second in the position of accusative as the object of «يُنَزِّل», and the third in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, with the preceding preposition-phrase as its khabar? There is disagreement. The first is the view of al-Akhfash, the second the view of al-Farrāʾ. On al-Farrāʾ's view the clause is a ṣifa of «جبال», so its position is judged to be genitive by considering the form, or accusative by considering the position.
It is also possible that «فيها» alone is the description, with «مِنْ بَرَدٍ» an agent of it because of its reliance, that is: it is settled in it.
Al-Zajjāj said: "Its meaning is: and He sends down from the sky, of mountains of hail in it, as you say: «هذا خاتمٌ في يدي من حديدٍ», that is, an iron ring on my hand. You brought «مِنْ» in this and in the verse when you separated, and because when you say «هذا خاتمٌ مِنْ حديدٍ» and «خاتمٌ حديدٍ» the meaning is one." End of quotation. So «مِنْ بَرَدٍ» would be in the position of genitive as a ṣifa / of «جبال», just as «من حديد» was a ṣifa of «خاتم», and the object of «يُنَزِّل» would be «من جبال». It follows from the mountains being hail that what is sent down is hail.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The second view: that the implied form is 'something of mountains', so the described noun was omitted and the description sufficed. This view is the correct one, because His saying {فِيهَا مِن بَرَدٍ} requires an object to which the pronoun returns, so its implied form would be: 'and He sends down from the mountains of the sky mountains in which there is hail'. In that there is extra omission, and an implication that can be dispensed with." There is room for objection in his words, because the pronoun has something to return to, namely «السماء», so there is no need to imply anything else, since that can be dispensed with, and there is nothing preventing it from returning to «السماء». His last words «and an implication that can be dispensed with» contradict his saying «this view is the correct one». The pronoun in «به» may return to the hail, which is the apparent view, and may return to both the wadq and the hail, the pronoun being treated like a demonstrative, as if it were said: "so He strikes with that"; a parallel has already been given in several places.
His saying: {سَنَا بَرْقِهِ}: the majority read «سَنا» short, which means light; it belongs to the verbs with wāw as third radical; one says «سَنا يَسْنُو سَناً», that is: it shone, it shines. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
3454 - يضيءُ سَناه، أو مصابيحُ راهِبٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Its light shines, or the lamps of a monk...)
And «السَّنا» with madd means loftiness. He said:
3455 - وسِنٍّ كسُنَّيْقٍ سَناءً وسُنَّماً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
Ibn Wathāb read «سَناءُ بُرَقِه» with madd, and with ḍamma on the bāʾ of «بُرَقِه» and fatḥa on the rāʾ. It is also reported from him with ḍamma on the rāʾ. As for the reading with madd, he compared the perceptible lightning, because of its height in the air, with the imperceptible [loftiness] of a human being. As for «بُرَقِه», it is the plural of «بُرْقَة», which is a measure of lightning, like «قُرَب». As for the ḍamma on the rāʾ, it is an ittibāʿ (vowel harmony), like «ظُلُمات» with ḍamma on the lām following the ḍamma of the ẓāʾ, although its original is sukūn.
The majority also read «يَذْهَبُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the hāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the hāʾ, from «أَذْهَبَ». Al-Akhfash and Abū Ḥātim declared this reading mistaken, saying: "because the bāʾ alternates with the hamza."
Their rejection is not correct, because it can be analysed in the way that the mutawātir reading {تُنْبِتُ بالدهن} [المؤمنون: 20] was analysed: that the bāʾ is additional, or that the object is omitted and the bāʾ has the meaning of «مِنْ», the implied form being: "He removes the light from the eyes", as in his saying:
3456 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... شُرْبَ النَّزِيف بِبَرْدِ ماءِ الحَشْرَجِ
(...the drinking of one drained of blood from the cool water of al-Ḥashraj.)

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {مِّن مَّآءٍ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is attached to «خَلَق», that is: He created every creature from water. «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range. On this it is said: there exist creatures that were not created from water, like Adam, who was from earth, and ʿĪsā, who was from a spirit, and the angels, who are from light, and the jinn, who are from fire. The reply was that the prevailing case is that. There is room for objection in this, since the angels are many times the number of animals, and the jinn too are many times their number. It was also said: because an animal cannot live except by it, it was made from it for that reason, although among animals there are some that do not need water at all, such as the ḍabb (spiny-tailed lizard).
It is also said: it is reported in exegesis that at first He created a jewel, looked at it, and it melted into water, and from it He created that. The second view: that «مِنْ» is attached to an omitted element as a ṣifa (adjective) of «دابَّة», and the meaning is the report that He created every creature that is from water, that is: every creature from water is created by Allah the Exalted. Al-Qaffāl said this.
He made «ماء» indefinite here, and made it definite in His saying {مِنَ المآء كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ} [الأنبياء: 30], because what is intended here is classification.
His saying: {فَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَمْشِي} to the end: He applied «مَنْ» to the non-rational because of its mixture with the rational in what is being detailed with «مَنْ», namely «كلَّ دابة»; using «مَنْ» was preferable for the agreement of the wording. It is also said: since He described them with what rational beings are described by, namely walking, He applied «مَنْ» to them. There is room for objection in this, because this attribute is not specific to rational beings, unlike His saying the Exalted: {أَفَمَن يَخْلُقُ كَمَن لاَّ يَخْلُقُ} [النحل: 17]. [And his saying:]
3457 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . هل مَنْ يُعِيْرُ جناحَه ... لَعَلِّي. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
the verse. The disagreement of the readers over {خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَآبَّةٍ} has already been given in Sūrat Ibrāhīm. "Walking" is borrowed for crawling on the belly, just as «المِشْفَر» (the camel's lip) is borrowed for the lip «الشَّفَة», and the reverse.

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {لِيَحْكُمَ}: the pronoun is singular although two nouns precede it, namely Allah and His Messenger, so it is like His saying the Exalted: {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ} [التوبة: 62], [because] the ruling of His Messenger is His ruling. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is like your saying «أعجبني زيدٌ وكَرَمَهُ»", that is, the generosity of Zayd. / And from it:
3458 - ومَنْهَلٍ من الفَلا في أوسَطِهْ ... غَلَسْتُه قبل القَطا وفُرَّطِهْ
(Many a watering place in the middle of the desert, I reached it in the dark before the sandgrouse and their advance parties.)
that is: before the advance party of the sandgrouse, meaning before the sandgrouse went ahead.
Abū Jaʿfar read «ليُحْكَمَ بينَهم» here and in the one after it as a passive, with the adverbial standing in the place of the agent.
His saying: {إِذَا فَرِيقٌ}: «إذا» is the one of surprise (fujāʾiyya). The precise treatment of it has already been given. It is the apodosis of the conditional «إذا» at the beginning. This is one of the proofs for preventing the apodosis from operating in the conditional «إذا»; for what follows the «إذا» of surprise does not operate on what precedes it. Thus the Shaykh mentioned it. The exposition of this has already preceded, along with the reply of the majority to it.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {إِلَيْهِ}: it may be attached to «يَأْتُوا», because «أتى» and «جاء» are both attested as transitive with «إلى». It may also be attached to «مُذْعِنين», because it has the meaning of "hastening in obedience". Al-Zamakhsharī held this correct, saying: "because its complement is placed first and indicates restriction". «مُذعِنين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-idhʿān is submission; one says: «أَذْعَنَ فلانٌ لفِلان», that is, he submitted to him. Al-Zajjāj said: "Al-idhʿān is hastening together with obedience."

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {أَمِ ارتابوا أَمْ يَخَافُونَ}: «أَمْ» in both is munqaṭiʿa (disconnected), which according to the majority is implied as a particle of rejection plus the interrogative hamza. Its implied form is: "rather, have they doubted; rather, do they fear?" The meaning of the question here is affirmation and confrontation, and it is sometimes used to intensify blame, as in his saying:
3459 - ألَسْتَ من القومِ الذينَ تعاهَدُوْا ... على اللُّؤْمِ والفَحْشاءِ في سالفِ الدهر
(Are you not of the people who pledged one another to baseness and indecency in past ages?)
and sometimes to intensify praise, as in the saying of Jarīr:
3460 - أَلَسْتُمْ خيرَ مَنْ ركبَ المَطايا ... وأندى العالمينَ بُطونَ راحِ
(Are you not the best of those who have ridden camels, and the most generous of all people, with the palms of your hands?)
And [his saying:] {أَن يَحِيفَ} is the object of the fear. Al-ḥayf is inclination and injustice in judgement. One says: «حاف في قضائِه», that is, he inclined.

semin-durr:51-51.t: His saying: {إِنَّمَا كَانَ قَوْلَ المؤمنين}: the majority put it in the accusative as the khabar of «كان», and the ism (subject) is the maṣdarī «أنْ» and what follows it. The Commander of the Faithful, al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it in the nominative as the ism, with «أَنْ» and what falls within its scope as the khabar. According to them [the grammarians] this is the weaker option, because whenever two definite nouns come together, it is preferable to make the more definite one the ism, although Sībawayh allowed a choice between any two definite nouns and did not draw this distinction. The precise treatment of this has already been given in Āl ʿImrān.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {وَيَتَّقْهِ}: the readers, with regard to the qāf, are on two levels. First: sukūn on the qāf, which only Ḥafṣ read; the others read it with kasra. With regard to the pronoun hāʾ, they are on five levels. First: giving it a vowel, detached, by one account; Warsh, Ibn Dhakwān, Khalaf, Ibn Kathīr and al-Kisāʾī read this. Second: sukūn on it, by one account; Abū ʿAmr and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read this. Third: sukūn on the hāʾ or joining it with a yāʾ; Khallād read this. Fourth: giving it a vowel without joining; Qālūn and Ḥafṣ read this. Fifth: giving it a vowel, joined or shortened; Hishām read this.
As for the sukūn of the hāʾ, its shortening and its lengthening, their treatment has been given fully in several places of this work. As for the sukūn of the qāf, they treated the detached as the attached: they put sukūn on the ʿayn of the pattern «فَعِل», saying «كَبْد» and «كَتْف» and «صَبْر» for «كَبِد» and «كَتِف» and «صَبِر», because it is a single word, and then what resembles that among detached forms was treated like the attached; for «يَتَّقْهِ» yields «تَقِهِ», like «كَتِف», and so it is given sukūn as those are. And from it:
3461 - قالَتْ سليمى اشْتَرْ لنا سَوِيقا
(Sulaymā said: buy us some barley gruel)
with sukūn on the rāʾ; just as another put sukūn in:
3462 - فبات مُنْتَصْباً وما تَكَرْدَسا
(He spent the night standing, not having crouched.)
and another:
3463 - عَجِبْتَ لمَوْلُودٍ وليسَ له أَبُ ... وذي وَلَدٍ لم يَلْدَهُ أبوان
(You marvel at one born who has no father, and at one with a child whom two parents did not beget.)
He means: «مُنْتَصِباً» and «لم يَلِدْه». The exposition of this rule has already been given at the beginning of al-Baqara, in His saying {فَهِيَ كالحجارة} [الآية: 74], and «وهي» and «وهو» and the like.
Makkī said: "It would have been necessary for whoever put sukūn on the qāf to put ḍamma on the hāʾ; for the pronoun hāʾ, when what precedes it is sākin and the sākin is not a yāʾ, takes ḍamma, as in «مِنْهُ» and «عَنْهُ». But since the sukūn of the qāf was incidental, it was not counted, and he left the hāʾ with the kasra it had with the kasra of the qāf, and did not join it with a yāʾ, because the omitted yāʾ before the hāʾ is implied and intended, so the omission that is in the yāʾ before the hāʾ remained on its original footing." Al-Fārisī said: "The kasra on the hāʾ is due to the meeting of two sākin letters, and is not / the kasra that precedes the ṣila; for the pronoun hāʾ is sākin in his reading, and when «تَقْهِ» was treated like «كَتْف» and the qāf was given sukūn, two sākin letters met, and when they met he was compelled to put a vowel on one of them: either the first or the second. There is no way to vowel the first, because that would return to what he fled from, namely the heaviness of «فَعِل»; so he vowelled the second. The basis of the meeting of two sākin letters is kasra, so for that reason he put kasra on the hāʾ. This is supported by his saying:
. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . لم يَلْدَه أَبَوانِ
for its original is «لَمْ يلِده» with kasra on the lām and sukūn on the dāl for the jussive; then when the lām was given sukūn two sākin letters met, and had he vowelled the first, it would have returned to what he fled from, so he vowelled the second, the dāl, and gave it fatḥa, though that is against the basis of the meeting of two sākin letters, in consideration of the fatḥa of the yāʾ."
Al-Qāsim ibn Fīrruh rejected al-Fārisī's view, saying: "His saying that he put kasra on the hāʾ because of the meeting of two sākin letters is not correct, because Ḥafṣ never gives the hāʾ sukūn in his reading."
Abū ʿAbd Allāh, the commentator on his qaṣīda, rejected this rejection, saying: "I am amazed at his denying sukūn from him when it is established from him in «أَرْجِهْ» and «فَأَلْقِهْ»; and if he reads it so in «أَرْجِهْ» and «فَأَلْقِهْ», it is possible that «يَتَّقْهِ» with him before the sukūn of the qāf was likewise, and this is perhaps strengthened by what is established from ʿĀṣim, his reading it with sukūn on the hāʾ together with kasra on the qāf."
I say: al-Shāṭibī did not mean that he never gave the hāʾ sukūn, the hāʾ as such, but meant the hāʾ of «يَتَّقْهِ» specifically. Al-Shāṭibī also objected to the explanation I presented earlier from Makkī, saying: "His explaining the omission of the ṣila by the omitted yāʾ before the hāʾ being implied and intended, so that he remained on his original footing in omitting the ṣila after the hāʾ, is not sound, because he read «يُؤَدِّهي» and the like with the ṣila, and if he took into account what he said about implying the yāʾ before the hāʾ he would not have joined it." Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: "Though he read «يُؤَدِّهي» and the like with the ṣila, he read «يَرْضَهُ» without ṣila, so Makkī attached «يَتَّقْهِ» to «يَرْضَهُ» and made it among the cases in which he departed from its like, in following the transmitted report and combining the two dialects. This was preferred by him because the wording supports it. And since the qāf was in the ruling of being kasra-vowelled, by the evidence of the kasra of the qāf after it, it became as if it were «يَتَّقِهِ» with kasra on the qāf and the hāʾ without ṣila, like the reading of Qālūn and Hishām in one of his two forms, so he explained it by what explains their reading. Al-Shāṭibī preferred to take it on the more frequent of what he read, not on what is rare and scarce, so that required his explanation as he stated."

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying: {جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) substituting for the verb's own wording, since the original of «أُقْسِمُ باللهِ جَهْدَ اليمين» is: «أُقْسِمُ بجَهْدِ اليمينِ جَهْداً»; the verb was omitted and the maṣdar put forward, set in its place, annexed to the object, like {َضَرْبَ الرقاب} [محمد: 4]. Al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being: "striving hard in their oaths", like their saying: «أفعَلْ ذلك جَهْدَك وطاقَتَك» ("do that to the utmost of your effort and capacity"). Al-Zamakhsharī mixed the two views and made them one, saying after what I presented from him: "The ruling of this accusative is the ruling of the ḥāl, as if it were said: striving hard in their oaths." The discussion of {جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ} [الآية: 53] has already been given in al-Māʾida.
His saying: {طَاعَةٌ مَّعْرُوفَةٌ}: there are three views on its nominative. First: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, whose implied form is: "our matter is obedience" or "what is required is obedience". Second: that it is a mubtadaʾ, with an omitted khabar, that is: "more fitting" or "more appropriate". It has been stated that whenever the khabar is originally a maṣdar substituting for the verb's wording, its mubtadaʾ must be omitted, as in His saying: {صَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ} [يوسف: 18], and it does not appear except by necessity, as in his saying:
3464 - فقالَتْ على اسمِ اللهِ أَمرُك طاعةٌ ... وإنْ كُنْتُ قد كُلِّفتُ ما لم أُعَوَّدِ
(She said: in the name of Allah, your command is obedience, even if I have been charged with what I was not accustomed to.)
though there is disagreement on that. Third: that it is an agent of an omitted verb, that is: "let there be obedience" and "let obedience be found". This was held weak: because a verb is omitted only if something precedes that signals it, as in His saying: {يُسَبَّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بالغدو والآصال رِجَالٌ} [النور: 36] / in the reading of those who made it passive, that is: "men glorify Him"; or if a negation is answered with it, as in your saying «بلى زيدٌ» to one who said "no one stood"; or an interrogative, as in his saying:
3465 - ألا هَلْ أتى أمَّ الحُوَيْرِثِ مُرْسَلٌ ... بلى خالد إنْ لم تُعِقْه العَوائقُ
(Has a messenger come to Umm al-Ḥuwayrith? Yes, Khālid, if obstacles do not hold him back.)
The majority read «طاعةٌ» in the nominative, according to what has preceded. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and al-Yazīdī read it in the accusative by an implied verb, which is the original. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If it were read in the accusative it would be permissible in Arabic, as a maṣdar, that is: 'obey with obedience' and 'say a saying'. His saying the Exalted after it indicates this: {قُلْ أَطِيعُواْ الله}." I say: what he wished to be read has indeed been read, as its transmission has preceded. As for his saying «{قُولُواْ قَوْلاً}», it is as if his tongue slipped to the verse of fighting, which is {فأولى لَهُمْ طَاعَةٌ وَقَوْلٌ مَّعْرُوفٌ} [محمد: 21], but the accusative there is impossible or far-fetched.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying: {فَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ}: it may be a past verb, with the wāw being the pronoun of the third-person plural. In the speech there would then be an iltifāt (shift) from address to the third person. What makes the shift good here is that He did not confront them with turning away and aversion. It may also be an imperfect, one of whose two tāʾs has been omitted, the original being «تَتَوَلَّوْا». This is supported by the reading of al-Bazzī with shadda on the tāʾ: «فإنْ تَّوَلَّوْا», although some of them consider it weak for combining two sākin letters not within their limit.
It is also supported by the address in His saying: {وَعَلَيْكُمْ مَّا حُمِّلْتُمْ وَإِن تُطِيعُوهُ تَهْتَدُواْ}. The claim of a second shift, from the third person to address, is far-fetched.

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying: {لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is the answer to an implied oath, that is: "I swear, He will surely make them successors", and the object of the promise is omitted, its implied form being: "He promised them succession", as indicated by His saying {لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ}. The second: that «وعد» is treated like an oath because of its certainty, so it is answered with what an oath is answered with.
His saying: {كَمَا استخلف}, that is: a succession like their succession. The majority build «اسْتَخْلَفَ» as an active verb. Abū Bakr built it as a passive. The relative noun is accusative on the first, nominative on the second.
His saying: {وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُمْ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū Bakr read «ولَيُبْدِلَنَّهم» with sukūn on the bāʾ and without shadda on the dāl, from «أَبْدَلَ». Its explanation has already been given in al-Kahf, in His saying: {أَن يُبْدِلَهُمَا رَبُّهُمَا} [الكهف: 81].
His saying: {يَعْبُدُونَنِي}: there are seven views on it. First: that it is a resumptive clause, that is, an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: "What is their state, that they are made successors and given security?" and it was said: "They worship Me." Second: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "they worship Me"; this clause too is resumptive and requires praise. Third: that it is a ḥāl from the object of «وَعَدَ اللهُ». Fourth: that it is a ḥāl from the object of «لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ». Fifth: that it is a ḥāl from its agent. Sixth: that it is a ḥāl from the object of «لَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُمْ». Seventh: that it is a ḥāl from its agent.
His saying: {لاَ يُشْرِكُونَ}: it may be resumptive; it may be a ḥāl from the agent of «يَعْبُدُونَنِي», that is: they worship Me as monotheists; and it may be a badal (substitute) for the preceding clause that occurs as a ḥāl, and what it involves has already been given.

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying: {وَأَقِيمُواْ الصلاة}: there are two views on it. One: that it is conjoined to {أَطِيعُواْ الله وَأَطِيعُواْ الرسول} [الآية: 54]. It is not far-fetched for a separation to occur between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined, however long, because the conjoined must be other than that to which it is conjoined. Al-Zamakhsharī said this. I say: his words "because the conjoined must" to the end do not appear to be a reason for the ruling he claimed. The second: that His saying {وَأَقِيمُواْ} is an instance of iltifāt (shift) from the third person to address. What makes it good is the address in His saying before that, «منكم».

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His saying: {لاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ}: the majority read «لا تَحْسَبنَّ» with the tāʾ of address. The agent is the pronoun of the addressee, that is: "do not think, O addressee". It is impossible or far-fetched to make it refer to the Messenger, peace be upon him, because / such a thought cannot be imagined from him so that he would be forbidden it. Ḥamza and Ibn ʿĀmir read «لا يَحْسَبَنَّ» with the yāʾ of the third person, and it is a good, clear reading. The agent in it is an implied pronoun referring to what the context indicates, that is: "let no thinker, or no one, think", or else referring to the Messenger because he was mentioned earlier. But that is weak because of the meaning mentioned before, contrary to those who declared the reciter of this reading to have made a grammatical error (laḥḥana), such as Abū Ḥātim, Abū Jaʿfar and al-Farrāʾ. Al-Naḥḥās said: "I know of no one among the people of Arabic, Basran or Kufan, except that he faults the reading of Ḥamza. Some of them say: it is an error because it brings only one object for «يَحْسَبَنَّ»."
Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is weak", but he allowed it with omission of the second object. The implied form: "Let those who disbelieve not think themselves able to frustrate". I say: the reason for their faulting this reading is that they believed «الذين» to be the agent, and there was in the wording only one object, namely «معجزين», so they said what they said. The reply to that is in several ways. One of them: that the agent is an implied pronoun referring to what preceded, or to what is understood from the context, as its exposition has preceded. The second: that the first object is omitted, its implied form being: "Let those who disbelieve not think themselves able to frustrate". However, omission of one of the two objects is weak according to the Basrans. And from it is the saying of ʿAntara:
3466 - ولَقَدْ نَزَلْتِ فلا تَظُنِّي غيرَه ... مني بمَنزِلَة المُحَبِّ المُكْرَمِ
(You have indeed taken your place, so think nothing else of me than that you are in the position of the honoured beloved.)
that is: "do not think anything else to be so". When al-Zamakhsharī took this view, he said: "Or the original may be: «لا يَحْسَبَنَّهم الذين كفروا مُعْجِزين», then the pronoun that is the first object was omitted. It is as if what allowed that is that, since the agent and the two objects belong to one thing, mentioning two sufficed in place of mentioning the third." So he implied the first object as an attached pronoun. The Shaykh said: "We rejected this analysis at the end of Āl ʿImrān, in His saying {لاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ الذين يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَآ أَتَوْاْ}, in the reading of those who read it with the third person and made the agent «الذين يَفْرحون». Its summary: this is not one of the pronouns that what follows them explains, so «لا يَحْسَبَنَّهم» is not to be implied, since «ظَنَّه زيدٌ قائماً» is not permissible with «زيدٌ» in the nominative as agent of «ظنَّه»." I say: the rejection of this rejection was already given in the place mentioned, so turn to it.
Third: that the two objects are His saying {مُعْجِزِينَ فِي الأرض}. The Kufans said this. When al-Zamakhsharī took this view, he said: "The meaning: let those who disbelieve not think anyone to be frustrating Allah on earth such that they would hope for the like of that themselves. This is a strong, excellent meaning."
I say: it was said to be an error, because the apparent point is that «في الأرض» is attached to «مُعْجِزين», and making it a second object is like preparing [the word] for the operation and then cutting it off from it; it is parallel to «ظَنَنْتُ قائماً في الدار».
His saying: {وَمَأْوَاهُمُ النار}: there are three views on it. First: that this clause is conjoined to the prohibition clause before it, without interpretation or implication, which is the school of Sībawayh, I mean conjoining clauses to one another even if their kinds differ among statement, request and performative. Its treatment and proof were given at the beginning of this subject. Second: that it is conjoined to it, but by interpreting the prohibition clause as a declarative clause. The implied form: "Those who disbelieve cannot escape Allah, and their abode is the Fire." Al-Zamakhsharī said this. It is as if he regards the correspondence of clauses as a condition for conjunction; this is the apparent state of his view. Third: that it is conjoined to an implied clause.
Al-Jurjānī said: "It is not possible that «ومَأْواهم» is connected to His saying «لا تَحْسَبَنَّ» — that is, this is an affirmation — so it is then conjoined by the wāw to an implied element before it, whose implied form is: 'do not think that those who disbelieve can frustrate on earth; rather they are overpowered, and their abode is the Fire'."

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is accusative as a time adverbial, that is: three times (of day); then He explained those times by His saying: {مِّن قَبْلِ صلاوة الفجر وَحِينَ تَضَعُونَ} {وَمِن بَعْدِ صلاوة العشآء}. The second: that it is accusative as a maṣdar, that is: three requests for permission. The Shaykh preferred this, saying /: "The apparent sense of «ثلاثَ مرات» is three requests for permission, because when you say «ضربْتُ ثلاثَ مراتٍ» you understand from it only three blows. It is supported by his saying, peace be upon him: 'Asking permission is three times.'" I say: it is granted that the apparent sense is so, but this apparent sense is abandoned because of the indicator mentioned, namely the explanation by the three times mentioned. Al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, read «الحُلْمَ» with sukūn on the ʿayn, which is the Tamīmī dialect.
His saying: {مِّن قَبْلِ صلاوة}: there are three views on it. First: that it is a badal (substitute) for His saying «ثلاث», so it is in the position of accusative. Second: that it is a badal for «عورات», so it is in the position of genitive. Third: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "they are from before", that is, those times, so it is in the position of nominative.
His saying: {مِّنَ الظهيرة}: there are three views on it. One: that «مِنْ» is for clarifying the genus, that is: the time of that which is the noon. Second: that it has the meaning of «في», that is: you put them off at noon. Third: that it has the meaning of the lām, that is: because of the heat of noon. As for His saying {وَحِينَ تَضَعُونَ}, it is conjoined to the position of {مِّن قَبْلِ صلاوة الفجر}, and His saying {وَمِن بَعْدِ صلاوة العشآء} is conjoined to what precedes it. Al-ẓahīra is intense heat, and it is the middle of the day.
His saying: {ثَلاَثُ عَوْرَاتٍ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr read «ثلاثَ» in the accusative; the others in the nominative. The first admits of three views. One, which is the apparent one: that it is a badal of His saying {ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ}. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The badal is correct only by implying: the times of three ʿawrāt, so the muḍāf is omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi is put in its place." Al-Ḥawfī, al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ also implied it so. It is possible that he made the three times themselves the three ʿawrāt by way of emphasis, so there is no need to omit a muḍāf. On this view, I mean the view of badal, it is not permissible to pause before {ثَلاَثُ عَوْرَاتٍ}, because it is a badal of it and follows it, and one does not pause on the followed without its follower.
Second: that {ثَلاَثُ عَوْرَاتٍ} is a badal of the times mentioned. Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. He means His saying {مِّن قَبْلِ صلاوة الفجر} and what is conjoined to it, and it is a badal in respect of the position; hence it is accusative.
Third: that it is accusative by an implied verb. Abū al-Baqāʾ implied "I mean". Better than this implication is "beware" or "guard against" three.
As for the second [reading], «ثلاثُ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, whose implied form is: "they are three ʿawrāt". Abū al-Baqāʾ implied it with the omission of a muḍāf, saying: "that is: they are the times of three ʿawrāt, so the mubtadaʾ and the muḍāf were omitted." I say: it may not be needed, by making the ʿawrāt themselves the times by way of emphasis, and that is what is understood from al-Zamakhsharī's words, though he implied it as a muḍāf, as I presented from him earlier.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He called each of these states an ʿawra because people's covering and guardedness lapse in them. Al-ʿawra is a defect (khalal), and from it come «أَعْوَرَ الفارِسُ» (the horseman exposed a gap) and «أَعْوَرَ المكانُ» (the place became exposed). And al-aʿwar is one whose eye is defective." This statement of his signals that «أوقات» is not implied as annexed to «عَوْراتٍ», unlike his first statement. Two views are thus taken from the sum of his words. On the nominative reading, and on the two views before it in analysing the accusative reading, one pauses before {ثَلاَثَ عَوْرَاتٍ}, because it is not a follower of what precedes it.
Al-Aʿmash read «عَوَرات» with fatḥa on the wāw, which is the dialect of Hudhayl and Banū Tamīm: they put fatḥa on the ʿayn of «فَعَلات» whether wāw or yāʾ. And it was recited:
3467 - أخو بَيَضاتٍ رائحٌ متأوِّبٌ ... رفيقٌ بمَسْحِ المَنْكِبينِ سَبُوْحُ
(The possessor of eggs, going out in the evening and returning, gentle in the stroking of his two shoulders, a swift swimmer.)
His saying: {لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ}: this clause may have a position in the iʿrāb, namely nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «ثلاث عَوْرات» in the reading of those who put it in the nominative, as if it were said: "they are three ʿawrāt specified by the absence of asking permission"; and it may have no position, being rather speech that confirms the command to ask permission in those states specifically, and that is in the reading of those who put «ثلاثَ عَوْراتٍ» in the accusative.
His saying: {بَعْدَهُنَّ}: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The implied form is: after their asking permission in them; then the preposition and the agent were omitted, leaving: after their asking permission; then the maṣdar was omitted." By agent he means the pronoun to which the asking permission is annexed, for it is a semantic agent of the maṣdar. This is not apparent; rather what / appears is that the meaning: there is no blame upon you or upon them, that is, the slaves, the maidservants and the children, in the absence of asking permission after these mentioned times, and there is no need for the implication he mentioned.
His saying: {طوافون} is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, whose implied form is: "they are those who go round", and «عليكم» is attached to it.
His saying: {بَعْضُكُمْ على بَعْضٍ}: there are three views on «بعضُكم». First: that it is a mubtadaʾ and «على بعض» is the khabar; Abū al-Baqāʾ implied it as "goes around among others". This clause would be a badal of what precedes it. It may also be confirmatory and explanatory. He means: it gave the same benefit as the clause before it, so it is a badal or a confirmation. The Shaykh rejected this: since it is a specific "being" [predicate], it may not be omitted. The reply: omission is prevented when nothing indicates it and the intent is to put the preposition-phrase in its place; here there is an indicator and no intent to put the preposition-phrase in its place; for that reason al-Zamakhsharī said: "its khabar is «على بعض», in the sense: one going round among others, and it was omitted because «طَوَّافون» indicates it."
Second: that it is nominative as a badal of «طوَّافون». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The Shaykh said: "It is not correct if the pronoun is made a third-person pronoun, by implying the mubtadaʾ «هم», because the implied form becomes: 'they: some of you go round among others', which is not correct. If you make the implied form: 'you: some of you go round among others', it is countered by the fact that His saying «عليكم» indicates that they are those gone round to, while 'you are those who go round' indicates they are the ones going round, so they conflict."
I say: we choose that the implied form is «أنتم», and no objectionable consequence follows. As for his saying "it is countered" to the end, there is no conflict in it, because the meaning is: each of you and of your slaves goes round among his fellow, even if the going round of one type is not the going round of the other, since what is meant is access to the states of the person; and «بعضُكم» would be a badal of «طَوَّافون». It was also said: «بعضُ» is a badal of «عليكم» with repetition of the operator, so you substituted a nominative for a nominative and a genitive for a genitive. A parallel is the poet's saying:
3468 - فلمَّا قَرَعْنا النَّبْعَ بالنَّبْعِ بعضَه ... ببعضٍ أبَتْ عِيدانُه أَنْ تكَسَّرا
(When we knocked nabʿ wood against nabʿ wood, part of it against part, its shafts refused to break.)
Here «بعضُه» is a badal of the accusative «النبعَ», and «ببعض» is a badal of the noun governed by the bāʾ.
Third: that it is nominative by an implied verb, that is: "some of you go round among others", omitted because «طَوَّافون» indicates it. Al-Zamakhsharī said this.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «طوَّافين» in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of «عليهم».

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying: {والقواعد}: the plural of «قاعِد» without the tāʾ of the feminine. Its meaning: those who have sat out of marriage, or out of menstruation, or out of enjoyment, or out of pregnancy, or out of all of these. Were it not for their being specified by that, the tāʾ would be obligatory, as in «ضارِبة» and «قاعِدة» from the familiar sense of sitting. His saying {مِنَ النسآء} and what follows is an explanation of them, and «القواعدُ» is the mubtadaʾ. «من النساء» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «اللاتي» is a ṣifa of «القواعد», not of «النساء». His saying {فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِنَّ}: the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the fā' entered because the mubtadaʾ is described by a relative; if that relative were the mubtadaʾ, its entry in its khabar would be allowed. For that reason I disallowed «اللاتي» being a ṣifa of «النساء», since there would be no justification left for the fāʾ entering the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The fāʾ entered because of the sense of condition in the mubtadaʾ, since the alif and lām have the meaning of «الذي»." This is the school of al-Akhfash, and its treatment was given in al-Māʾida. But here there is something that makes that unnecessary: namely what I mentioned, the description of the mubtadaʾ by the mentioned relative.
{غَيْرَ مُتَبَرِّجَاتِ} is a ḥāl from «عليهنَّ». Al-tabarruj is appearing, from al-burj, which is the conspicuous building. «بزينةٍ» is attached to it.
His saying: {وَأَن يَسْتَعْفِفْنَ} is a mubtadaʾ by interpretation: "their abstaining", and «خيرٌ» is its khabar.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {أَوْ مَا مَلَكْتُمْ مَّفَاتِحهُ}: the majority read with fatḥa on / the mīm, and the lām without shadda. Ibn Jubayr read «مُلِّكْتُم» with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the lām with shadda, that is: someone else gave you ownership. The majority read «مفاتحَه» without yāʾ, the plural of «مِفْتَح». Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that it be the plural of «مِفْتَح» with kasra, which is the instrument, and that it be the plural of «مَفْتح» with fatḥa, which is the maṣdar, meaning opening. Ibn Jubayr read «مفاتيحَه» with yāʾ after the tāʾ, the plural of «مِفْتاح». The first is more analogical. Abū ʿAmr, in the transmission of Hārūn from him, read «مِفتْاحَه» in the singular, and it is the reading of Qatāda.
His saying: {أوْ صَدِيقِكُمْ}: the majority read with fatḥa on the ṣād. Ḥumayd al-Khazzāz transmitted kasra on it, as vowel harmony with the kasra of the dāl. Al-ṣadīq applies to the singular and the plural, like «الخَليط» and «القَطِين» and their like.
His saying: {جَمِيعاً} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the subject of «تَأْكُلوا», and «أَشْتاتاً» is conjoined to it; it is the plural of «شَتّ».
His saying: {تَحِيَّةً} is accusative as a maṣdar from the meaning of «فسَلِّموا», so it belongs to the chapter of «قَعَدْتُ جُلوساً». The pattern of «التحيَّة» has already been given. {مِّنْ عِندِ الله} may be attached to an omitted element as a ṣifa of «تحيةً», and it may be attached to «تحيِّة» itself, that is: the greeting issuing from Allah's side. «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range, figuratively; however, it clouds the description that an explicit ṣifa is placed after an interpreted one. What is in it has already been given.

semin-durr:62-62.t:
His saying: {على أَمْرٍ جَامِعٍ}: «جامع» is a figurative attribution (isnād majāzī); since it was a cause of their gathering, the act was attributed to it figuratively. Al-Yamānī read «على أَمْرٍ جميعٍ», and it may be an intensive form meaning «مُجَمِّع», or it may not. The conditional clause of His saying {وَإِذَا كَانُواْ} together with its apodosis is conjoined to the ṣila in His saying «آمَنوا».
His saying: {لِبَعْضِ شَأْنِهِمْ} is a reason, that is: for the sake of some of their need. The majority pronounce the ḍād clearly before the shīn, while Abū ʿAmr assimilated it into it because of the closeness between them, as the ḍād is from the farthest edge of the tongue and the shīn from its middle. A group of grammarians considered this transmission weak and thought it unlikely from Abū ʿAmr, the head of the craft, because the ḍād is stronger than the shīn, and the stronger is not assimilated into the weaker. Al-Zamakhsharī treated its transmitter, al-Sūsī, badly.
People have replied, saying: "The ground for the assimilation is that the shīn has greater elongation than the ḍād, and has breath that the ḍād lacks, so the ḍād has become less than it, and assimilating the lesser into the greater is permissible." He said: "This is supported by Sībawayh's report from some of the Arabs of «اطَّجَعَ» for «اضْطجع»; and if its assimilation into the ṭāʾ is permissible, its assimilation into the shīn is more fitting." The opponent does not concede all that was mentioned, and the ground for objection is clear.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying: {دُعَآءَ الرسول}: this maṣdar (verbal noun) may be annexed to its object, that is: "your calling the Messenger", in the sense that you do not call him by his name, saying "O Muḥammad", nor by his kunya, saying "O Abū al-Qāsim", but call and address him with reverence: "O Messenger of Allah, O Prophet of Allah". A large group held this view. It may also be annexed to the agent. People's expressions differed on this meaning. It was said: do not make his calling you like one of you calling another, so that you are slow to respond to him, as one of you is slow toward another when he calls him for something; rather you must hasten to his command. Abū al-ʿAbbās preferred this, and it is supported by His saying: {فَلْيَحْذَرِ الذين يُخَالِفُونَ عَنْ أَمْرِهِ}. It was also said: its meaning is: do not make the Messenger's supplication to his Lord like the way your young supplicates your old, or your poor your rich, asking him for a need, so that perhaps his call is answered and perhaps not; the supplications of the Messenger, peace be upon him, are heard and answered... [Translator's note: the source text breaks off here with «في التخريجة الأخرى» ("in the other analysis"); it is translated as written.]
Al-Ḥasan read «نَبِيِّكم» with the nūn placed before the bāʾ, which has kasra, followed by a doubled genitive yāʾ, in place of the adverbial «بينَكم» of the majority reading. There are three views on it. One: that it is a badal (substitute) of «الرسول». Second: that it is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it, because «النبي» [is a messenger], and by being annexed to the addressees it became better known than «الرسول». Third: that it is a naʿt (adjective). It is not to be said that this is impermissible because this, as you have established, is more definite, and an adjective is not more definite than what it describes, but rather less or equal; for «الرسول» has become a proper name, by predominance, for Muḥammad ﷺ, so the two are equal in definiteness.
His saying: {قَدْ يَعْلَمُ الله}: «قد» with the imperfect indicates fewness except in the acts of Allah the Exalted, where it indicates certainty, as in this verse. Some returned it to fewness but in respect of what the knowledge is attached to, meaning that those who do that are few; so the fewness is not in the knowledge but in its object.
His saying: {لِوَاذاً}: there are two views on it. One: that it is accusative as a maṣdar from the meaning of the first verb, since the implied form is: "they slip away from among you stealthily", or "they take cover, taking cover". The second: that it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, that is: taking cover. «اللِّواذُ» is the maṣdar of «لاوَذَ». The wāw remained sound although what precedes it has kasra, and it was not changed to yāʾ as it was changed in «قيام» and «صِيام», because it remained sound in the verb, as in «لاوَذَ»; had it been weakened in the verb, it would be weakened in the maṣdar, as in «القيام» and «الصِّيام», because it was changed into alif in «قام» and «صام». As for the maṣdar of «لاذَ بكذا يَلُوْذُ به» / it is weak, as in «لاذَ لِياذاً», like «صام صِياماً» and «قام قِياماً». «اللِّواذُ» and «المُلاوَذَةُ» mean concealing oneself; one says «لاَوَذَ فلانٌ بكذا», that is, he concealed himself by it. «اللَّوْذُ» is what surrounds the mountain. It was also said: «اللِّواذُ» is dodging from one thing to another in secrecy. In exegesis: the hypocrites used to go out concealed among the people without asking permission so that they would not be seen. The pattern «مفاعلة» is because each of them takes cover with his companion, so mutuality exists.
Yazīd ibn Quṭayb read «لَواذاً» with fatḥa on the lām, and it admits two views. One: that it is the maṣdar of the triliteral «لاذ», so it is like «طاف طَوافاً».
And it can be the maṣdar of «لاوَذَ», except that the first radical was given fatḥa as vowel harmony with the fatḥa of the ʿayn; this is a weak explanation, fit for a reading like this.
His saying: {فَلْيَحْذَرِ الذين}: there are two views on it. The better known, and the only one the grammarians recognise: that the relative is the agent and «أن تصيبَهم» is its object, that is: "let those who oppose His command beware lest a trial befall them". The second: that the agent of «فَلْيَحْذَرْ» is a latent pronoun, and the relative is a direct object. This has been rejected on several grounds. Among them: that implication is contrary to the basic rule. There is room for objection, because this implication is equivalent to what is pronounced, so it cannot be said that it is contrary to the basic rule. Do you not see that in «قُمْ» and «ولْتقم» the agent is latent, and it is not said of any of that that it is contrary to the basic rule? Implication is contrary to the basic rule only where it is an omission, as in {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [يوسف: 82].
Among them: that this pronoun has no antecedent, that is, there is nothing it refers to, so it is invalid for the agent to be a latent pronoun. The reply: that what the pronoun refers to is the first relative, that is: "let the slipping-away ones beware of those who oppose His command", so they are commanded to beware of them, that is, commanded to avoid them as one is commanded to avoid the sinners. They rejected this on two grounds. One: that the pronoun is singular and what it refers to is plural, so the agreement which is a condition in explaining pronouns is lost. Second: that the slipping-away ones are the opposers; so if they were commanded to beware of those who oppose, they would be commanded to beware of themselves, which is not permissible, since they cannot be commanded to beware of themselves.
The first can be answered: that the pronoun, though singular, refers to a plural on the consideration that the meaning is: "let him beware", that is, of mentioning the like of that. Sībawayh related «ضرَبني وضربْتُ قومَك», that is: "he who is there and he who was mentioned struck me", which is a known question in grammar; or the implied form is: "let each one of the slipping-away ones beware". The second: it is permissible for a person to be commanded figuratively to beware of himself, meaning that he not obey it in its desires and the evil it prompts him to. It is as if it were said: "let the opposers beware of their selves, and not obey them in what they command them"; for this reason one says «أَمَر نفسَه ونهاها» (he commanded and forbade his soul) and «أَمَرَتْه نفسُه» (his soul commanded him), by figurative consideration.
Among them: that His saying {أَن تُصِيبَهُمْ فِتْنَةٌ أَوْ يُصِيبَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ} becomes loose and lost; because «يَحْذَرُ» takes one object, which on your claim it has already taken, namely «الذين يُخالفون», and it does not take two such that they could say «أنْ تصيبَهم فتنةٌ» is in the position of its second object; so it remains lost. There is room for objection, for its loss is not conceded, since it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). It was objected to this: that it has not fulfilled the conditions for the accusative because of the difference of agent, as the agent of the caution is other than the agent of the befalling. This is weak, because omission of the preposition is regular with «أَنْ» and «أنَّ». We say: it is granted that the conditions for the accusative are absent, and it is governed by the lām in implication, and the lām was omitted with «أَنْ» only because of its length with the ṣila.
«يُخالِفُون» takes its object directly, as in «خالَفْتُ أَمْرَ زيدٍ», and with «إلى», as in «خالَفْتُ إلى كذا»; so how did this one take the preposition of departure (ʿan)? There are several views. One: that it is made to imply the meaning of «صَدَّ» and «أَعْرَضَ», that is: he turned away from His command and averted from it while opposing it. Second: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its meaning is that their opposition occurs after / His command, as you say: «كان المطر عن ريحِ كذا» ('the rain came after such-and-such wind'), and «عَنْ» is for what is beyond the thing." Third: that it is redundant, that is: they oppose His command; al-Akhfash and Abū ʿUbayda took this view, and redundancy is contrary to the basic rule.
It has been read «يُخَلِّفون» with shadda, and its object is omitted, that is: they leave themselves behind.

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His saying: {قَدْ يَعْلَمُ مَآ أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "He introduced «قد» to emphasise His knowledge of what they are upon, of opposition to the religion and hypocrisy, and the emphasis of the knowledge returns to emphasising the threat. That is because «قد», when it enters the imperfect, has the sense of «رُبَّما», so it agrees with «رُبَّما» in passing into the sense of multiplicity, as in his saying:
3469 - فإنْ تُمْسِ مهجورَ الفِناءِ فرُبَّما ... أقامَ به بعدَ الوُفودِ وُفودُ
(If you end up with a deserted courtyard, then often after delegations have departed, other delegations have stayed in it.)
and similar to that is the saying of Zuhayr:
3470 - أخي ثقةٍ لا تُهْلِكُ الخمرُ مالَه ... ولكنَّه قد يُهْلِكُ المالَ نائِلُهْ
(A trustworthy brother, whose wealth wine does not destroy, but his generosity may well destroy wealth.)
The Shaykh said: "That «قد», when it enters the imperfect, gives multiplicity is the view of some grammarians. It is not correct; the multiplicity is understood from the context. The correct view is that «رُبَّ» is for lessening of the thing, or lessening of its like. If multiplicity is understood, it is from the context, not from it."
{وَيَوْمَ يُرْجَعُونَ}: there are two views on «يوم». One: that it is a direct object and not an adverbial, because it is conjoined to His saying {مَآ أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ}, that is: He knows what you are upon of all your states, and He knows the day they are returned, like His saying: {إِنَّ الله عِندَهُ عِلْمُ الساعة} and {لاَ يُجَلِّيهَا لِوَقْتِهَآ إِلاَّ هُوَ}. The second: that it is an adverbial for something omitted. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The implied form may be: 'and the knowledge apparent to you, or the like, on the day', so the accusative is as an adverbial." End of quotation.
The majority read «يُرْجَعون» as a passive. Abū ʿAmr, with others, read it as an active. On both readings two views are possible. One: that there is in the speech an iltifāt (shift) from address in His saying {مَآ أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ} to the third person in «يُرْجَعون». The second: that «ما أنتم عليه» is a general address to everyone, and the pronoun in «يُرْجَعُون» is for the hypocrites specifically, so there is then no shift.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {سُورَةٌ أَنزَلْنَاهَا}: two views are possible for its nominative. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause after it is its adjective, which is what licenses beginning with an indefinite noun. As to the khabar there are two views. The first: that it is the clause of His saying {الزانية والزاني}. Ibn ʿAṭiyya inclined to this, for he said: "It may be a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar {الزانية والزاني} and what comes after it. The meaning: the revealed, obligatory sūra is such-and-such, since a sūra is an expression for a series of verses having a beginning and an end." The second: that the khabar is omitted, i.e. «فيما يُتْلَى عليكم سورةٌ» ("among what is recited to you is a sūra") or «فيما أَنْزَلْنا سورةٌ» ("among what We sent down is a sūra").
The second of the first two views: that the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is implied, i.e. «هذه سورةٌ» ("this is a sūra"). Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«سورةٌ» in the nominative on the implication: «هذه سورةٌ», or «مِمَّا يُتْلى عليك سورةٌ», so «سورةٌ» is not a mubtadaʾ because it is indefinite." This is a difficult expression as it stands. How can he say "it is not a mubtadaʾ" while implying «فيما يُتْلى عليك سورةٌ»? And how can he justify the prohibition by its being indefinite while implying for its khabar a preposition and genitive noun placed before it, which is itself a licence for beginning with an indefinite?
The majority read it in the nominative as above. Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī, ʿĪsā al-Kūfī, Mujāhid and Abū Ḥaywa, among others, read «سورةً» in the accusative. There are several views on it. The first: that it is accusative by an implied verb not explained by what follows it, its implied form being «اتْلُ سورةً» or «اقرأ سورةً» ("recite a sūra"). The second: that it is accusative by an implied verb explained by what follows it; the matter is one of ishtighāl; its implied form: «أَنْزَلْنا سورةً أنزلناها». The difference between the two views: the clause after «سورةً» is in the accusative position on the first, and has no position on the second. The third: that it is accusative as an incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. «دونَكَ سورةً» ("take a sūra"). Al-Zamakhsharī said this, and the Shaykh rejected it, because the particle of incitement may not be omitted. The Shaykh also found the permissibility of beginning with an indefinite without a licence problematic on the ishtighāl view. The meaning of that: there is no place where the accusative by ishtighāl is permitted but the nominative as mubtadaʾ is also permitted; and here, if «سورة» were put in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, it would not be permissible, since there is no licence. So one does not say «رجلاً ضربتُه», because «رجلٌ ضربتُه» is impossible. Then he answered: if the omission of an adjective is assumed it is permissible, i.e. «سورة مُعَظَّمة» or «مُوَضَّحة أَنْزَلْناها» ("an honoured / clarified sūra We sent down"); then that is permissible.
The fourth: that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the «ها» in «أَنْزِلْناها», and a ḥāl from a pronoun may be placed before it; al-Farrāʾ said this. On this the pronoun in «أَنْزَلْناها» does not refer to the sūra but to the rulings, as if it were said: "We sent down the rulings as a sūra of the sūras of the Qur'an", so these rulings are established by the Qur'an, unlike others, which are established by the Sunna.
His saying: {وَفَرَضْنَاهَا}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it with doubling [of the rā᾽]; the rest lightened. The doubling is either for intensification of the obligation and emphasis, or for the multiplicity of those on whom it is obligatory, or for the multiplicity of the thing made obligatory. The lightened form means "We made it obligatory and made it categorically binding".

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {الزانية والزاني}: there are two views on their nominative. The school of Sībawayh: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. «فيما يُتْلَى عليكم حكمُ الزانية» ("among what is recited to you is the ruling on the adulteress"). Then He explained that with His saying {فاجلدوا} to the end. The second, the school of al-Akhfash and others: it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is the imperative clause. The fāʾ entered because the mubtadaʾ resembles a condition. The discussion of this question has already been given exhaustively at His saying {واللذان يَأْتِيَانِهَا مِنكُمْ فَآذُوهُمَا} [al-Nisāʾ: 16] and at His saying {والسارق والسارقة} [al-Māʾida: 38], so there is no need to repeat it.
ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī, Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and Ruways read them in the accusative, by ishtighāl. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is better than «سورةً أنزلناها» because of the imperative. And «واللذَّانِ» has been read without the yāʾ."
His saying: {رَأْفَةٌ}: the majority read here, and in [Sūrat] al-Ḥadīd, with sukūn on the hamza, and Ibn Kathīr with fatḥa. Ibn Jurayj, and it is also related from Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim, read «رَآفة» with an alif after the hamza, on the pattern of «سَحابة»; all of them are maṣdars of «رَأَفَ به يَرْؤُف». Its meaning has already been given. The best known of the maṣdars is the first. Abū l-Baqāʾ reported a fourth dialect in it, which is the substitution of the hamza by alif. The like of this is obvious and needs no pointing out, for it is an independent dialect and a mutawātir reading.
The majority read «تَأْخُذْكم» with the feminine, in regard to the wording. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, al-Sulamī and Mujāhid [read it] with the yāʾ, because the feminine is figurative and because of the separation by the object and the preposition phrase. «بهما» is attached to «تَأْخُذْكم», or to an omitted element by way of clarification; it is not attached to «رَأْفة», because a maṣdar's governed element may not precede it. And «في دين الله» is also attached to the verb before it. This clause indicates the apodosis of the condition after it, or, according to some, it is the apodosis.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {وَحُرِّمَ ذلك}: Abū l-Barhasam read «وحرَّم» in the active, with doubling. Zayd ibn ʿAlī [read] «وحَرُمَ» on the pattern of «كَرُم».

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {والذين يَرْمُونَ المحصنات}: like His saying {الزانية والزاني فاجلدوا} [al-Nūr: 2], so what preceded there returns here unchanged. As for His saying {المحصنات}, there are two views on it. The first: that women only are meant, and He singled them out for mention because slandering them is more heinous. The second: that women and men are meant; on this it is asked: how did He give priority to the feminine over the masculine? The answer: that it is an adjective of an omitted thing that includes men and women, i.e. «الأنفسَ المحصناتِ» ("the chaste souls"), but this is remote. Or you say: there is an omitted conjoined word, understood from the meaning, and consensus holds that their ruling is the ruling of the women, i.e. «والمُحْصَنين» ("and the chaste men").
His saying: {بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَ}: the majority annex the numeral to the counted noun. Abū Zurʿa and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim read the numeral with tanwīn.
