People found this reading very eloquent, until some, such as Ibn Jinnī, went beyond the limit, preferring it to the majority reading; he said: "because whenever the counted noun is an adjective, following (ittibāʿ) is better than annexation. You say «عندي ثلاثةُ ضاربون», and «ثلاثةُ ضاربين» is weak." This is a mistake, because an adjective that has come to function as nouns is given their ruling, so the numeral is annexed to it, and «شهداء» is of that kind, for the omission of its described noun is frequent. The Exalted said: {مِن كُلِّ أمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ} and {واستشهدوا شَهِيدَيْنِ} [al-Baqara: 282], and you say «عندي ثلاثةُ أَعْبُدٍ», and all of these are adjectives in origin.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported from Sībawayh that he does not permit tanwīn of the numeral except in poetry; it is not as he reported from him. Sībawayh said that only about nouns, such as «ثلاثةُ رجالٍ»; as for adjectives, the distinction mentioned above applies to them.
On this reading, concerning {شُهَدَآءَ} there are three views. The first: that it is a tamyīz. This is invalid, because from three to ten the numeral is annexed to its specified noun and nothing else, and anything else is a necessity [of poetry]. The second: that it is a ḥāl, which is also weak, because of its coming from an indefinite without a specifier. The third: that it is genitive as an adjective of «أربعة», and is a diptote because of the feminine alif.
His saying: {وأولئك هُمُ الفاسقون}: this clause may be resumptive, which is the more apparent; Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted it to be a ḥāl.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ الذين تَابُواْ}: there is disagreement about this exception: does it return to the clauses before it, or to the last clause only? Among the grammarians Ibn Mālik and al-Mahābādhī spoke about it. Ibn Mālik chose its return to the preceding clauses, and al-Mahābādhī to the last. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The rejection of the slanderer's testimony is, according to Abū Ḥanīfa (may Allah have mercy on him), contingent on the full execution of the ḥadd punishment. So if he testifies [to it] before the ḥadd or before its execution is completed, his testimony is accepted. Once it has been executed, his testimony is never accepted, even if he repents and is among the pious righteous. According to al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him), the rejection of his testimony is tied to the slander itself; so if he repents of the slander by retracting it, he returns to being one whose testimony is accepted. Both rely on the verse: Abū Ḥanīfa (may Allah have mercy on him) made the consequence of the condition, which is the accusation, the flogging and the rejection of testimony following the flogging, in perpetuity, so they are ones whose testimony is rejected for the whole of their 'forever', which is their lifetime; and he made His saying {وأولئك هُمُ الفاسقون} a resumptive statement not within the scope of the consequence of the condition, as if it were a report of the state of the accusers before Allah after the conditional clause had finished, and {إِلاَّ الذين تَابُواْ} an exception from «الفاسقين». His saying {فَإِنَّ الله غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ} indicates this. Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him) also made the two clauses the consequence of the condition, except that he directed 'forever' to the duration of his being a slanderer, which ends with repentance [and retraction] from the slander, and he made the exception attached to the second clause." End of quotation. I mentioned the ruling only because the i'rab depends on it.
As for the position of the excepted, there are three views. The first: that it is accusative on the basic rule of exception. The second: that it is genitive as a badal from the pronoun in «لهم»; al-Zamakhsharī made this clear with his saying: "The right of the excepted according to him, i.e. al-Shāfiʿī, is to be genitive as a badal from «هم» in «لهم», while its right according to Abū Ḥanīfa is to be accusative, because it follows an affirmative. What the apparent sense of the verse and its composition require is that the three clauses together be the consequence of the condition, as if it were said: whoever slanders chaste women, flog them, reject their testimony and declare them transgressors — that is, combine for them the flogging, the rejection and the declaring of transgression — except those who repent of the slander and reform, for Allah forgives them, so they come out neither flogged, nor rejected, nor declared transgressors." The Shaykh said: "The apparent sense of the verse does not require the exception to return to the three clauses; rather the apparent view, which Arab usage supports, is the return to the clause that immediately follows it."
The third view: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause of His saying {فَإِنَّ الله غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ}. This was objected to because the clause lacks a link. It was answered that the link is omitted, i.e. «غفورٌ لهم». They also disagreed about this exception: is it connected or disconnected? The second is very weak.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُمْ شُهَدَآءُ إِلاَّ أَنفُسُهُمْ}: there are two views on the nominative of «أنفسهم». The first: that it is a badal from «شهداء»; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned no other in the course of his speech. The second: that it is an adjective of it, on the basis that «إلاَّ» means «غير». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Were it read in the accusative it would be permissible, as the khabar of «كان», or accusative as an exception. The nominative is stronger here because «إلاَّ» here is an adjective of the indefinite, as we mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Anbiyāʾ." I say: on the nominative reading it is possible that «كان» is the defective one, with the preposition phrase as its khabar, and that it is the complete one, i.e. "there were found no witnesses for them".
The majority read «يكن» with the yāʾ (masculine), which is the eloquent form, because when the verb is attributed to what follows «إلاَّ» in the manner of tafrīgh (exclusive exception), the masculine in the verb is obligatory according to some, as in «ما قام إلاَّ هندٌ», and «ما قامَتْ» is not permissible except in necessity, as in the saying:
3433 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
وما بَقِيَتْ إلاَّ الضلوعُ الجَراشعُ
("and nothing remained but the broad ribs"),
or in an irregularity, such as the reading of al-Ḥasan: «لا ترى إلاَّ مَساكنُهم». «ولم تَكُنْ» has also been read with the tāʾ (feminine), and you have learned what is in that.
His saying: {فَشَهَادَةُ أَحَدِهِمْ}: there are three views on its nominative. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is an implied one placed first, i.e. «فعليهم شهادة» ("upon them is a testimony"), or placed last, i.e. «فشهادة أحدِهم كافيةٌ» or «واجبةٌ» ("one of them's testimony is sufficient / obligatory"). The second: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. «فالجوابُ شهادةُ أحدِهم» ("the remedy is one of them's testimony"). The third: that it is the agent of an implied verb, i.e. «فيكفي» ("it suffices"). The maṣdar here is annexed to its agent.
The majority read «أربعَ شهاداتٍ» in the accusative as a maṣdar. The operator in it is «شهادة»; the governor of the maṣdar is a maṣdar like it, as was mentioned at His saying {فَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ جَزَآؤُكُمْ جَزَاءً مَّوْفُوراً} [al-Isrāʾ: 63]. The two brothers and Ḥafṣ read «أربع» in the nominative, as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, which is His saying «فشهادة».
On the two readings the attachment of the preposition phrase in His saying «بالله» is explained. On the accusative reading three views are possible. The first: that it is attached to «شهادات», because it is nearer to it. The second: that it is attached to His saying «فشهادةُ», i.e. «فشهادةُ أحدِهم بالله». The separation by «أربع» does no harm, because it is a governed element of the maṣdar, so it is not foreign. The third: that the question belongs to the chapter of tanāzuʿ (competition between two operators); each of «شهادة» and «شهادات» seeks it in terms of meaning, and the question is one of applying the second operator with omission from the first, which is the choice of the Basrans. On the nominative reading its attachment to «شهادات» is necessary, since if you attached it to «شهادة» it would entail separation between a maṣdar and its governed element by a foreign element, which is not permissible. There is no disagreement about the second «أربع», in His saying «أَنْ تَشْهد أربعَ شهاداتٍ», that it is accusative, because the operator in it is stated explicitly, namely the verb.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {والخامسة}: the Seven agreed on the nominative of the first «الخامسة» and disagreed about the second: Ḥafṣ put it in the accusative, and al-Ḥasan, al-Sulamī, Ṭalḥa and al-Aʿmash put both in the accusative. The nominative is as a mubtadaʾ, with «أنَّ» and what is in its scope as the khabar. As for the accusative of the first, on the reading of those who put «أربعَ شهادات» in the accusative, the accusative is by conjunction to the accusative before it; and on the reading of those who put it in the nominative, the accusative is by an implied verb, i.e. «ويَشْهَدُ الخامسةَ». As for the accusative of the second, it is a conjunction to the accusative before it, namely «أربع شهادات». The accusative here is stronger than in the first, because of the strength of the accusative in what precedes it, as was established; for that reason there is no disagreement in it. As for «أنَّ» and what is in its scope: on the nominative reading it is in the nominative position as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, as before; on the accusative reading it is by dropping of the preposition, and the preposition is attached to that governor of «الخامسة», i.e. «ويشهد الخامسةَ بأنَّ لعنةَ الله وبأنَّ غضبَ اللهِ». Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted it to be a badal from «الخامسة».
His saying: {أَنَّ لَعْنَةَ الله عَلَيْهِ}: the majority read «أنَّ» doubled in both places. Nāfiʿ read it lightened in both places, except that he reads «غَضِبَ اللهُ», making «غَضِبَ» a past verb with the Majestic Name as its agent. The Shaykh thus reported from him the lightening in the first place too, and no one else reported it. On his reading the noun of «أنْ» is the pronoun of the matter in both places, «لعنةُ الله» is a mubtadaʾ, «عليه» its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «أنْ». In the second, «غضِبَ الله» is a verbal clause in the position of the khabar of «أنْ» as well; but it is said: one of two things is incumbent on you: either no separation between the lightened [«أنْ»] and the verb serving as khabar, or the occurrence of a request as khabar in this chapter, which is impermissible. The explanation of that: when the khabar of the lightened [«أنْ»] is a fully conjugated verb not accompanied by «قد», separation between them is obligatory, by what was given in [Sūrat] al-Māʾida. If it is answered that it is a supplication, it is objected that supplication is a request, and they have stated explicitly that request clauses do not occur as the khabar of «إنَّ», so that they interpreted the verses:
3434 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... إنَّ الرِّياضةَ لا تُنْصِبْك للشَّيْبِ
("... Indeed training will not wear you out for old age")
and:
3435 - إنَّ الذينَ قَتَلْتُمْ أمسِ سَيِّدَهُمْ ... لا تَحْسَبوا ليلَهم عن ليلِكم ناما
("Indeed those whose chief you killed yesterday — do not think their night has slept apart from yours")
on the implication of "saying". Similar is {أَن بُورِكَ مَن فِي النار} [al-Naml: 8]. Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Qatāda, al-Sulamī and ʿĪsā read «أنْ» lightened and «غَضَبُ الله» in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the preposition phrase after it its khabar, and the clause the khabar of «أنْ».
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "And the lightened «أنْ» on the nominative reading is in His saying «أَنْ غَضِبَ», and the verb follows it. Abū ʿAlī said: 'The grammarians find it ugly for a verb to follow it unless something separates between it and the verb, as in His sayings {عَلِمَ أَن سَيَكُونُ} [al-Muzzammil: 20] and {أَفَلاَ يَرَوْنَ أَلاَّ يَرْجِعُ} [Ṭāhā: 89]. As for His saying {وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلإِنسَانِ} [al-Najm: 39], that is because of «ليس» being little established among verbs. As for His saying {أَن بُورِكَ مَن فِي النار}, «بُوْرِكَ» is in the sense of supplication, so the separator did not come, lest the meaning be spoiled.'" I say: the apparent sense of this is that «غَضِبَ» is not a supplication but a report, as in «غَضَِبَ الله عليها». The apparent view is that it is a supplication, just as «بُورك» is; the meaning is not a report in either. So Abū ʿAlī's objection, and Abū Muḥammad's following of him, are not satisfactory.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {وَلَوْلاَ فَضْلُ الله}: the apodosis of «لولا» is omitted, i.e. «لَهَلَكْتُمْ» ("you would have perished").

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {إِنَّ الذين جَآءُوا بالإفك}: there are two views on the khabar of «إنَّ». The first: that it is «عُصْبةٌ», with «منكم» its adjective. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "By it the khabar is made informative." The second: that the khabar is the clause of His saying {لاَ تَحْسَبُوهُ}, and «عُصْبَةٌ» is a badal from the agent of «جاؤوا». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The implied form is: 'the act of those who ...'. This is more consistent in meaning and more beneficial than «عُصبةٌ» being the khabar of «إنَّ»." The Shaykh cited it so from him, without objecting to him. The objection to it is plain: he made the khabar of «إنَّ» a request clause, and it has already been said that this is not permissible, and whatever of it occurs in poetry is interpreted, like the two verses above. Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied that muḍāf before the relative so that the composition of the speech might be sound, for had he not implied it the composition would have been «لا تَحْسَبوهم». According to Ibn ʿAṭiyya the pronoun in «لا تَحْسَبوه» does not refer to «الإفك», lest the clause be without a link tying it to the mubtadaʾ. According to others it may refer to the «الإفك», or to the slander, or to the maṣdar understood from «جاؤوا», or to what befell the Muslims of distress.
His saying: {كِبْرَهُ}: the majority read the kāf with kasra, and it was read with ḍamma by al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī, Abū Rajāʾ, Abū l-Barhasam, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, Mujāhid and ʿAmra bint ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and it was also related from Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī. It is said that they are two dialects in the maṣdar of «كَبُرَ الشيءُ», i.e. became great; but it has prevailed in usage that the ḍamma form is for age and rank, one says «هو كُبْرُ القومِ» with ḍamma, i.e. the eldest of them in age or rank. In the ḥadīth, in the story of Muḥayyiṣa and Ḥuwayyiṣa: «الكُبْرَ الكُبْرَ» ("the eldest, the eldest"). It is also said: the ḍamma is the greater part of the slander, and the kasra the beginning of it. And it is said: with kasra it is the sin.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {لولا إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ المؤمنون}: this «لولا» is of exhortation (taḥḍīḍ), and «إذ» is accusative by «ظَنَّ». The implied form: «لولا ظَنَّ المؤمنين بأنفسِهم إذ سَمِعْتُموه» ("why did the believers not think well of themselves when you heard it"). In this speech there is a shift of person (iltifāt). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said «لولا إذ سَمِعْتُموه ظَنَنْتُمْ بأنفسِكم خيراً وقُلْتم»? And why did He turn from the second person to the third, and from the pronoun to the overt noun? I say: to make the rebuke emphatic by way of iltifāt, and to state the word 'belief' explicitly, as an indication that sharing in it requires that no one should believe a statement against his brother." His saying "why did He turn from the address?" means in His saying «وقالوا», since the original would have been «وقلتم», so He turned from this address to the third person in «وقالوا». And his saying "and from the pronoun" means that the original would have been «ظَنَنْتُمْ», so He turned from the pronoun of address to the word «المؤمنين».

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {فَإِذْ لَمْ يَأْتُواْ}: «إذْ» is accusative by «الكاذبون» in His saying {فأولئك عِندَ الله هُمُ الكاذبون}. This speech has the force of a condition and its consequence.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ}: «إذْ» is accusative by «مَسَّكُمْ» or by «أَفَضْتُمْ». The majority read «تَلَقَّوْنه». The original is «تَتَلَقَّوْنه», and one of the two tāʾs was dropped, like {تَنَزَّلُ} [al-Qadr: 4] and the like. Its meaning is that some of you receive it from others. Al-Bazzī follows his rule in doubling the tāʾ in continuous reading. Its investigation has already been given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara, as in {وَلاَ تَيَمَّمُواْ} [al-Baqara: 267]; there it was easier because what precedes it is a soft letter, unlike here. Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza follow their rules in assimilating the dhāl into the tāʾ. Ubayy read «تَتَلَقَّوْنَه» with two tāʾs, and it has been said that this is the original. Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ in one transmission from him read «تُلْقُوْنَه» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, sukūn on the lām and ḍamma on the qāf, imperfect of «ألقى إلقاءً». In another transmission he read «تَلْقَوْنه» with fatḥa on the tāʾ, sukūn on the lām and fatḥa on the qāf, imperfect of «لَقِيَ».
Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿĀʾisha, ʿĪsā, Ibn Yaʿmar and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ, kasra on the lām and ḍamma on the qāf, from «وَلَقَ الرجلُ» when he lies. Ibn Sīda said: "They brought the transitive as a witness for the intransitive. In my view he meant «تَلِقُوْن فيه», then the particle was dropped and the verb connected to the pronoun." He means that they brought «تَلِقُوْنه», which is transitive, explained by «تُكذِّبون», which is intransitive, and then he attributed to it what he mentioned. Al-Ṭabarī and others said: "This word is taken from «الوَلْق», which is hastening with one thing after another, like running after running and speech after speech. One says «وَلَقَ في سَيْرِه», i.e. he hastened," and he recited:
3436 - جاءَتْ به عَنْسٌ من الشَّأْمِ تَلِقْ ...
("A strong she-camel brought it from Syria, hurrying ...")
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "i.e. you hasten in it. Its origin is from «الوَلْق», which is madness."
Zayd ibn Aslam and Abū Jaʿfar read «تَأْلِقُوْنه» with fatḥa on the tāʾ, a quiescent hamza, a lām with kasra and a qāf with ḍamma, from «الأَلْق», which is lying. Yaʿqūb read «تِيْلَقُوْنه» with kasra on the tāʾ, followed by a quiescent yāʾ, a lām with fatḥa and a qāf with ḍamma; it is the imperfect of «وَلِق» with kasra on the lām, as they said «يِيجَلُ» as the imperfect of «وجِل».
His saying: {بِأَفْوَاهِكُمْ}: like His saying {يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْوَاهِهِم} [Āl ʿImrān: 167], which has already been given.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {ولولا إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ قُلْتُمْ}: like His saying {لولا إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ} [verse 12], but there is no iltifāt in it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is separation between «لولا» and «قُلْتم» permissible? I say: adverbials have a status that others do not have, because what occurs in them is inseparable from them, so latitude is allowed in them." The Shaykh said: "This suggests that the matter is peculiar to adverbials, but it also applies to the direct object; you say «لولا زيداً ضَرَبْتَ» and «لولا عمراً قَتَلْتَ»."
Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "If you say: what is the benefit of putting the adverbial first so that it falls as a separator? I say: the benefit in it is to make clear that it was incumbent on them to avoid speaking of the slander the first moment they heard it; so since mention of the time was more important, it was necessary to put it first. If you say: what is the meaning of «يكون», when the speech without it is straightforward had it been said «ما لنا أن نتكلَّم بهذا»? I say: its meaning is 'it is fitting and valid', i.e. it is not fitting and not valid, as in His saying {مَا يَكُونُ لي أَنْ أَقُولَ} [al-Māʾida: 116]."

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {أَن تَعُودُواْ}: there are three views on it. The first: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. "He admonishes you, disliking that you return". The second: that it is on the omission of «في», i.e. «في أَنْ تعودوا», as in «وَعَظْتُ فلاناً في كذا فتركه» ("I admonished so-and-so about such-and-such and he gave it up"). The third: that it includes the meaning of a verb that is made transitive by «عَنْ», which was then omitted, i.e. "He restrains you by admonition from returning". On these last two views the two views arise about the position of «أنْ» after the removal of the preposition.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {فَإِنَّهُ يَأْمُرُ}: there are three views about this hāʾ. The first: that it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); Abū l-Baqāʾ began with it. The second: that it is the pronoun of the Devil. These two views are permissible only according to those who do not require a pronoun returning to the conditional noun from the clause of the consequence. The third: that it refers to the conditional «مَن».
His saying: {مَا زَكَا}: the majority read the kāf lightened; one says «زكا يَزْكُو». In its alif, imāla is possible or not. Al-Aʿmash and Abū Jaʿfar read it doubled. Its alif is written as a yāʾ, which is irregular because it is of the wāw-roots like «غزا». It was carried over only to the dialect of those who use imāla, or to the writing of the doubled form. On the lightened reading «مِنْ أحد» is the agent; on the doubled reading it is the object. And «مِنْ» is redundant on both views. The agent is Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ يَأْتَلِ}: it may be «يَفْتَعِلُ» from «الأَلِيَّة», which is the oath, as in the verse:
3437 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . .
وآلَتْ حَلْفَةً لم تَحَلَّلِ
("and she swore an oath that she did not absolve").
Al-Zamakhsharī supported this with the reading of al-Ḥasan «ولا يَتَأَلَّ» from «الأَلِيَّة», as in the [ḥadīth] "whoever takes an oath against Allah, He will give him the lie". It may also be «يَفْتَعِلُ» from «أَلَوْتُ», i.e. "I fell short", as in the saying of the Exalted {لاَ يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبَالاً} [Āl ʿImrān: 118]. He said:
3438 - وما المرءُ ما دامَتْ حُشاشةُ نَفْسِه ... بمُدْرِكِ أَطْراف الخُطوب ولا آلِ
("A man, so long as a spark of life remains in him, neither attains the extremities of calamities nor falls short.")
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«ولا يَتَأَلَّ» has also been read, on the pattern yatafaʿʿal, and it is from «الأَلِيَّة» too."
I say: and from it:
3439 - تَأَلَّى ابنُ أَوْسٍ حَلْفَةً لِيَرُدَّني ... إلى نِسْوةٍ كأنَّهنَّ مَفائِدُ
("Ibn Aws swore an oath to return me to women who are like spits for roasting.")
His saying: {أَن يؤتوا}: it is on the dropping of the preposition, and its implied form on the first view is «ولا يَأْتَلِ أُولوو الفَضْلِ على أَنْ لا يُحِسنوا» ("let not those of virtue swear not to do good"); on the second: «ولا يُقَصِّر أُولو الفَضْل في أَنْ يُحِسنوا» ("let not those of virtue fall short in doing good"). Abū Ḥaywa, Abū l-Barhasam and Ibn Quṭayb read «تُؤْتُوا» with the tāʾ of address. It is an iltifāt that agrees with His saying «ألا تُحِبون». Al-Ḥasan and Sufyān ibn al-Ḥusayn read «وَلْتَعْفُوا وَلْتَصْفَحُوا» in the second person, which agrees with what follows it.

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ}: its governor is the settling (istiqrār) to which «لهم» is attached. It is also said: rather its governor is «عذابُ». This was rejected because it is a described maṣdar, and it was answered that latitude is allowed in the adverbial that is not allowed in other things. The two brothers read «يَشْهَدُ» with the yāʾ (masculine), because the feminine is figurative and a separation has occurred. The rest [read it] with the tāʾ, in regard to the wording.

semin-durr:25-25.t: The tanwīn in «إذ» is a substitute for a clause, its implied form being «يوم إذ تشهد» ("the day when it testifies"). The disagreement of al-Akhfash about it has already been given. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يُوْفِيْهِمْ» lightened, from «أوفى». The majority read «الحق» in the accusative as an adjective of «دينَهم», while Abū Ḥaywa, Abū Rawq and Mujāhid, and it is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd, read it in the nominative as an adjective of Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ}: it may be a resumptive clause, or in the nominative position as a second khabar; and it may be that «لهم» is the khabar of «أولئك» and «مغفرةٌ» its agent.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {تَسْتَأْنِسُواْ}: it may be from «الاستئناس» (seeking familiarity), because the one who knocks feels uneasy about whether he will be admitted or not, so his unease is removed; it is a synonym of asking permission, and so was put in its place. It is also said: from «الإيناس», which is perceiving, i.e. "until you find out the state of affairs". Ibn ʿAbbās explained it as «حتى تَسْتَأْذِنُوا» ("until you ask permission"), but that is not a reading. What is transmitted from him, that he said: "«تستأنسوا» is a scribe's mistake; it is only «تستأذنوا»" . . . . . is falsely ascribed to him. It is parallel to what was given earlier in [Sūrat] al-Raʿd, {أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الذين آمنوا} [al-Raʿd: 31], about which the discussion has been given.
[Translator's note: the source reads «إنما هون تستأذنوا»; «هون» is evidently a misprint for «هو».]
«والاستِئْناسُ» is seeking information. He said:
3440 - كأنَّ رَحْلِيْ وقد زال النهارُ بنا ... يومَ الجليلِ على مُسْتَأْنِسٍ وَحَِدِ
("As if my saddle, when the day had declined with us on the day of al-Jalīl, were on a wary, solitary [wild ox]").
It is also said: it is from «الإنْس» with kasra on the hamza, i.e. he finds out whether there is a human being in it or not. Al-Ṭabarī reported that it means «وتُؤْنِسُوا أنفسَكم» ("and put your selves at ease").
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The conjugation of the verb refuses to let it be from «آنسَ»."

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {أَن تَدْخُلُواْ}: i.e. «في أن تدخلوا» ("in that you enter"). The preposition phrase is attached to «جُناح».

semin-durr:30-30.t: His saying: {مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ}: there are several views about «مِنْ». The first: that it is partitive, because the first glance that occurs without intention is pardoned for the one looking. The second: that it is for stating the kind; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this, and there is something to consider in it, in that no vague term has preceded for «مِنْ» to explain. The third: that it is for the beginning of the range; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The fourth: that it is redundant; this is the statement of al-Akhfash.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {وَلْيَضْرِبْنَ}: «يَضْرِبْنَ» includes the meaning of «يُلْقِيْنَ» ("cast"), which is why it is made transitive by «على». Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read the imperative lām with kasra.
Ṭalḥa read «بخُمْرِهنَّ» with sukūn on the mīm; giving sukūn to [the pattern] fuʿul in the plural is preferable to giving sukūn to the singular. Ibn Kathīr, the two brothers and Ibn Dhakwān put kasra on the jīm of «جُيُوْبِهِنَّ».
«والغَضُّ» is the closing of the eyelid so that it prevents seeing. He said:
3441 - فَغُضِّ الطَرْفَ إنَّك مِنْ نُمَيْرٍ ... فلا كعباً بَلَغْتَ ولا كِلابا
("So lower your gaze, for you are of Numayr; you have reached neither Kaʿb nor Kilāb.")
«والخُمُر» is the plural of «خِمار». In the paucal it is pluralised as «أَخْمِرَة». Imruʾ al-Qays said:
3442 - وَتَرى الشَّجْراءَ في رَيِّقِهِ ... كَرُؤوسِ قُطِعَتْ فيها الخُمُرْ
("And you see the trees in its first flush like heads that have been cut off, with the head-coverings still on them.")
«والجَيْب» is what is in the collar of the shirt, from which part of the body shows.
His saying: {غَيْرِ أُوْلِي}: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read «غيرَ» in the accusative. There are two views on it: the first, that it is an exception; the second, that it is a ḥāl. The rest [read] «غيرِ» in the genitive as an adjective, or a badal, or a bayān. «والإِرْبَةُ» is need. Its derivation was given in [Sūrat] Ṭāhā.
His saying: {مِنَ الرجال}: a ḥāl from «أُولي». As for His saying «أو الطفلِ الذين», it was given in [Sūrat] al-Ḥajj that «الطفلَ» applies to the dual and the plural, which is why it was described in the plural. It is also said: since the class was intended, the plural was observed in it; so it is like their saying «أهلكَ الناسَ الدينارُ الحُمْرُ والدِّرْهَمُ البيضُ» ("the red dinars and the white dirhams have ruined people").
«وعَوْرات» is the plural of «عَوْرَة», which is what a person wishes to cover of his body, and it predominantly applies to the two private parts. The majority read «عَوْرات» with sukūn on the wāw, which is the dialect of the generality of the Arabs; they gave it sukūn for lightness, because of the weak letter. Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission read «عَوَرات» with fatḥa on the ʿayn [sic: the wāw]. Ibn Khālawayh reported that it is the reading of Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Aʿmash. It is the dialect of Hudhayl ibn Mudrika. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Some recited to me:
3443 - أخُو بَيَضاتٍ رائِحٌ متأوِّبُ ... رفيقٌ بمَسحِ المَنْكِبَيْنِ سَبُوحُ
("[A male ostrich,] father of eggs, going out in the evening and returning, gentle in stroking the two shoulders, swift-gliding.")
Ibn Mujāhid considered it a solecism and a mistake, meaning from the standpoint of transmission; otherwise it is an established dialect.
His saying: {أَيُّهَا المؤمنون}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the hāʾ and an alif after the hāʾ, being the «ها» of attention. Ibn ʿĀmir here, in [Sūrat] al-Zukhruf {ياأيها الساحر} [verse 49] and in [Sūrat] al-Raḥmān {أَيُّهَا الثقلان} [verse 31] read it with ḍamma on the hāʾ in continuous reading, and when he pauses he gives it sukūn. The reason: when the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, the fatḥa on a light letter was felt to be light, so the hāʾ was given ḍamma by assimilation. These three places have been written without an alif. Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī pause with an alif, and the rest without it, following the script and the agreement of writing with pronunciation; and it is retained elsewhere, in keeping with the original, as in {يَاأَيُّهَا الناس} [al-Baqara: 21] and {يَآأَيُّهَا الذين آمَنُواْ} [al-Baqara: 153]. In sum, the script is a followed tradition.
[Translator's note: in the second paragraph on «عَوَرات», the source says "fatḥa on the ʿayn", although the fatḥa that distinguishes this form falls on the wāw; the text is translated as printed.]

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {الأيامى}: the plural of «أيِّم», on the pattern fayʿil. From it one says «آمَ يَئِيْم», like «باع يبيع». The poet said:
3444 - كلُّ امرىءٍ سَتَئِيْمُ مِنْهُ ... العِرْسُ أو منها يَئِيْمُ
("Every man — his wife will become widowed of him, or he will become widowed of her.")
The regular plural of it would be «أيائم», like «سَيِّد» and «سِيائِد». As for «أيامى» there are two views. The more apparent, from the speech of Sībawayh, is that it is a plural on the pattern fiʿālā, not transposed, and likewise «يتامى». It is also said: the original is «أيايِم» and «يتايِم» for «أيِّم» and «يتيم», and they were transposed. «والأَيِّم» is one who has no spouse, male or female. Abū Bakr al-Khaffāf restricted it to a woman who has lost her husband, so its application to a virgin is figurative. «منكم» is a ḥāl, and likewise «مِنْ عبادِكم».

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {والذين يَبْتَغُونَ الْكِتَابَ}: the nominative is possible in it, as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar the clause joined with the fāʾ, because of the sense of condition that the mubtadaʾ includes. Its accusative is also possible, by an implied verb, on the basis of ishtighāl. This is preferable because of the imperative.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«آم» and «آمَتْ» and «تَأَيَّما» are said when the two have not married, whether both are virgins or previously married. He said:
3445 - فإن تنكِحي أنكِحْ وإن تتأيَّمي ... وإن كنتُ أفتى منكمُ أتَأَيَّمُ
('If you marry, I shall marry; and if you remain unmarried, I shall remain unmarried, though I am younger than you.')
And from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'O Allah, we seek refuge in You from ʿayma, ghayma, ayma, kazam and qaram.'" I say: as for «العَيْمَة» with the undotted ʿayn, it is intense craving for milk, and with the dotted ghayn [«الغَيْمة»] intense thirst. «والأَيْمة» is a long period of celibacy; «والكَزَم» is intense craving for eating; and «والقَرَمُ» is intense craving for meat.
His saying: {عَلَى البغآء}: «البغاء» is the maṣdar of «بَغَت المرأةُ تَبْغي بِغاءً», i.e. she committed fornication. It is specific to women's fornication. This condition has no implied contrary meaning, because compulsion does not coexist with willingness.
His saying: {فِإِنَّ الله}: a clause that occurs as the apodosis of the condition. The returning pronoun to the conditional noun is omitted, its implied form being «غفور لهم» ("forgiving to them"). Al-Zamakhsharī implied it in one of his implications, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū l-Baqāʾ [implied]: «فإنَّ اللهَ غفورٌ لهنَّ», i.e. for the women who are compelled; so the clause of the consequence is bare of a link tying it to the conditional noun. It is not said that the link is the implied pronoun that is the agent of the maṣdar, since the implied form is «مِن بعد إكراهِهم لهنَّ», so that this implied link would suffice; because they did not count that among the links. You say «هندٌ عجبْتُ مِنْ ضَرْبِها زيداً», and this is permissible; but if you said «هندٌ عجبتُ مِنْ ضَرْبِ زيدٍ», i.e. from her striking, it would be impermissible, because of its lacking a link even though it is implied.
Imām al-Rāzī weakened the implication of «بهم» and preferred the implication of «بهنَّ», saying: "There are two views on it. The first: forgiving to them (the women), because compulsion removes sin and punishment from the compelled person in what he did. The second: Allah is forgiving to the one who compels, on condition of repentance. This is weak, because on the first interpretation there is no need for this implication." There is something to consider in this, as you have learned that, according to the majority, a pronoun returning to the conditional noun is necessary, and its investigation was given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara. When al-Zamakhsharī implied «لهنَّ» he raised a question, saying: "If you say: there is no need to attach the forgiveness to them, because the woman compelled to fornication, unlike the one who compels [her to it], is not sinful. I say: perhaps the compulsion is something other than what the Sharia has taken into account, of compulsion by killing or by what one fears destruction or loss of a limb from, so that she is safe from sin. Perhaps she fell short of the limit within which she is excused, and so is sinful."

semin-durr:34-34.t:
The disagreement over «مُبَيّنات», with kasra and fatḥa, has already been given.
His saying: {وَمَثَلاً}: a conjunction upon «آيات», i.e. "and We sent down an example from the examples of those before you".

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {الله نُورُ السماوات}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar, either on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. «ذو نورِ السماوات» ("the possessor of the light of the heavens"), the light meaning His justice. His saying {مَثَلُ نُورِهِ} supports this. He annexed the light to these two containers, either as an indication of the breadth of His radiance and the spread of His illumination, so that the heavens and the earth are lit by it, or in order to mean the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, who are illumined by it. It is also possible that the expression is exaggerated by way of praise, as in their saying: "So-and-so is the sun of the lands and their moon." Al-Nābigha said:
3446 - فإنَّك شمسٌ والملوكُ كواكبٌ ... إذا ظهرَتْ لم يَبْدُ منهنَّ كوكبُ
("For you are a sun and the kings are stars; when it appears, not one of them shows.")
And he said:
3447 - قَمَر القبائلِ خالدُ بن يزيد ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
("The moon of the tribes is Khālid ibn Yazīd ...")
It is also possible that the maṣdar occurs in place of the active participle, i.e. «مُنَوِّرُ السماواتِ» ("illuminator of the heavens"). This view is supported by the reading of the Commander of the Faithful, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abū Jaʿfar and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Makkī: «نَوَّرَ» as a past verb, its agent the pronoun of the Creator the Exalted, «السماواتِ» its object, so its kasra is the accusative sign, and «الأرضَ» in the accusative is conjoined to it. Al-Ḥasan explained it, saying: "Allah is the illuminator of the heavens."
His saying: {مَثَلُ نُورِهِ كَمِشْكَاةٍ}: also a mubtadaʾ and khabar. This clause is a clarification and explanation of what precedes it, so it has no position. There is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «كَمَثَلِ نورِ مشْكاة». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. the description of His light, wondrous in its illumination, is like a niche, i.e. like the description of a niche."
They disagreed about the pronoun in «نُوره». It is said: it is for Allah the Exalted, and this is preferable, and the light on this view means the clear verses mentioned earlier, or faith. It is also said: it refers to the believers, or the believer, or whoever believed in Him. Ubayy read with all these wordings, and he returned the pronoun to what he read. It is also said: it refers to Muḥammad ﷺ, though no mention of these things has preceded. As for its referring to the believers in Ubayy's reading, there is a difficulty in respect of the singular. Makkī said: "One pauses at «الأرض» on these three views."
They also disagreed about this simile: is it a composite simile (tashbīh murakkab), i.e. the intention is to compare a whole with a whole, without regard to matching part with part, but the intention is to compare His guidance and the perfection of His craft in every created thing, as a whole, with this whole of the light that they make, which is the most eloquent attribute of light among you? Or a non-composite simile, i.e. the intention is to match part with part? The discussion about it is arranged according to the views on the pronoun in «نوره».
«والمِشْكاةُ» is a niche that does not go through. Is it Arabic, or Abyssinian and Arabicised? There is disagreement. It is also said: it is the iron or lead [vessel] in which the wick (dhubāl) is placed, and it is in the interior of the glass. It is also said: it is the pillar on whose top the lamp is placed. And it is said: the iron thing in which the lantern is hung. Al-Dūrī from al-Kisāʾī used imāla in «المِشْكاة» because of the preceding kasra, even though there is a separator. It is written with a wāw, like «الزكاة» and «الصلاة».
«والمِصْباح» is the large lamp. «والزجاجةُ» is the singular of «الزجاج», a well-known substance. It has three dialects: ḍamma is the dialect of the Hijaz and the reading of the majority; kasra and fatḥa are the dialect of Qays. Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim, in Ibn Mujāhid's transmission, read it with fatḥa. Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim in another transmission from him, and Abū Rajāʾ, read it with kasra. The disagreement is likewise in His saying «الزجاجةُ».
The clause of His saying {فِيهَا مِصْبَاحٌ} is an adjective of «مِشْكاة». It is also possible that the preposition phrase alone is the description and «مصباحٌ» is nominative by it as agent.
His saying: {دُرِّيٌّ}: Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read it with kasra on the dāl and a yāʾ followed by a hamza. Ḥamza and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read it with ḍamma on the dāl and a yāʾ followed by a hamza. The rest [read it] with ḍamma on the dāl and a doubled yāʾ without hamza. These three are among the Seven. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda read it with fatḥa on the dāl and a doubled yāʾ. Al-Zuhrī read it with kasra on it and a doubled yāʾ. Abān ibn ʿUthmān, Ibn al-Musayyab, Abū Rajāʾ and also Qatāda read «دَرِّيْء» with fatḥa on the dāl, a doubled rā᾽ and a yāʾ followed by a hamza.
As for the first, it is a clear reading because it is a pattern found often in nouns, such as «سِكِّين», and in adjectives, such as «سِكِّير».
As for the second reading, it is from «الدِّرْء», meaning pushing, i.e. its parts push one another, or its light pushes away its concealment. It is said that nothing is found on the pattern fuʿʿīl except «مُرِّيْق» (for safflower), and «سُرِّيَّة», on our view that it comes from «السرور», a yāʾ having been substituted for one of the doubled letters and the yāʾ of fuʿʿīl assimilated into it; and «مُرِّيخ» (for what is inside a dry horn), also said with kasra on the mīm; and «عُلِّيَّة», and «دُرِّيْء» in this reading, and «ذُرِّيَّة» too in one view. Some said: "The pattern of «دُرِّيْء» in this reading is fuʿʿūl, like «سُبُّوح» and «قُدُّوس»; the succession of ḍammas was felt heavy so it was shifted to kasra, and this is also transmitted in «سُرِّية» and «ذُرِّيَّة»."
As for the third reading, it admits two views. The first: that its origin has the hamza as in Ḥamza's reading, except that he substituted a yāʾ for the hamza and assimilated, so that the meaning of the two readings is one. It may also be a relational form (nisba) to «الدُّر» (pearl), for its purity and the clarity of its radiance.
As for the reading with a doubled yāʾ with fatḥa and kasra on the dāl, what appears is that it is related to «الدُّر»; the fatḥa and kasra on the dāl belong to the changes of nisba forms.
As for fatḥa on the dāl with madd and hamza, there is a difficulty in it. Abū l-Fatḥ said: "It is a rare pattern, of which only «السَّكِّينة» is preserved, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and doubling of the ʿayn." I say: and al-Akhfash reported: «فَعَلَيْه السَّكِّينة والوَقار» and «كوكَبٌ دَرِّيْءٌ» from «دَرَأْتُه».
His saying: {يُوقَدُ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «تَوَقَّدَ» on the pattern tafaʿʿala, a past verb in which there is a pronoun of its agent referring to the lamp, and not to «كوكب», because the meaning would be spoiled. The two brothers and Abū Bakr [read] «تُوْقَدُ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ (feminine) and fatḥa on the qāf, the imperfect of «أَوْقَدَ». It is passive, and the deputy agent is a pronoun referring to «زجاجة» that is latent in the verb. The rest of the Seven read likewise, except with the yāʾ (masculine); and the latent pronoun refers to the lamp.
Al-Ḥasan, al-Sulamī and Ibn Muḥayṣin read, and it is related from ʿĀṣim through al-Mufaḍḍal, likewise, except that he put ḍamma on the dāl, making it the imperfect of «تَوَقَّدَ»; the original is «تَتَوَقَّد» with two tāʾs, and one of them was dropped like «تَذَكَّرُ». The pronoun is also for the glass.
ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «وَقَّدَ», a past verb on the pattern of «قَتَّلَ», doubled, i.e. the lamp. Al-Ḥasan and Sallām also read «يَوَقَّدُ» with yāʾ and ḍamma on the dāl, the imperfect of «تَوَقَّدَ». The original is «يَتَوَقَّدُ» with yāʾ and tāʾ, and the tāʾ was dropped. This is irregular, since two identical letters did not occur in succession, and nothing remained in the wording to indicate what was dropped, unlike «تَنَزَّلُ» and «تَذَكَّرُ» and their type, in which there are two tāʾs and what remains indicates what is lost. A line of analogy may be strained to justify it, namely that they carried «أَعِدُ» and «تَعِدُ» and «نَعِدُ» over «يَعِدُ» in the omission of the wāw because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra; likewise they carried «يَتَوَقَّد» with yāʾ and tāʾ over «تَتَوَقَّد» with two tāʾs, even though the heaviness is not found in the yāʾ and tāʾ.
His saying: {مِن شَجَرَةٍ}: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range, and there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «مِنْ زيتِ شجرةٍ» ("from the oil of a tree"). Concerning «زَيْتونة» there are two views, of which the better known is that it is a badal from «شجرةٍ». The second: that it is an ʿaṭf bayān; this is the school of the Kufans, and Abū ʿAlī followed them. This has already been given at His saying {مِن مَّآءٍ صَدِيدٍ} [Ibrāhīm: 16].
His saying: {لاَّ شَرْقِيَّةٍ}: an adjective of «شَجَرة», and the «لا» entered to convey negation. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read it in the nominative, on the implication of a mubtadaʾ, i.e. «لا هي شرقيةٌ» ("it is not eastern"). The clause is also in the genitive position as an adjective of «شَجَرة».
His saying: {يَكَادُ}: this clause is also an adjective of «شجرةٍ».
His saying: {وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ}: its apodosis is omitted, i.e. «لأضاءَتْ» ("it would give light"), because of the indication of what precedes it, and the clause is a ḥāl clause. The investigation of this was given at the saying «رُدُّوا السَّائلَ ولو جاءَ على فَرَس» ("Turn the beggar away, even if he comes on a horse"), and that it is for covering all the states, even in this state. Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan read «يَمْسَسْه» with the yāʾ (masculine), because the feminine is figurative and because there is also a separation by the object.
His saying: {نُّورٌ على نُورٍ}: the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. «ذلك نورٌ» ("that is light"). And «على نورٍ» is an adjective of «نور».
